sections.subtitle: Kad svaki izbori postanu referendum: kraj vremena političke bezbrižnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović objašnjava kako su turbulentna zbivanja iz temelja promijenila svijet i politizirala građane
sections.content:
Podcast Radija Mrežnica i ovoga puta otvara geopolitičke teme. Voditeljica gošću, **Jadranku Polović**, predstavlja kao jednu od ponajboljih geopolitičkih analitičarki u regiji. Polović je politologinja i znanstvena suradnica, a doktorirala je iz područja međunarodnih odnosa, i to na temu odnosa SAD-a i regije.

Razgovor počinje slikovito. Voditeljica primjećuje da ni scenarist turbulentnog geopolitičkog filma ne bi smislio sadašnjost kakvu svijet trenutačno živi: izbori na kojima padaju i mali i veliki, novi ratovi koji prijete i stari koji ne završavaju. Od gošće traži da kroz „žensku geopolitičku intuiciju“ opiše vrijeme u kojem se živi.

Polović se vraća dva desetljeća unatrag. Tada bi se, kaže, u ovakvom razgovoru moglo reći da izbori i nisu osobito važni. Ljudi nisu bili apolitični, ali su živjeli u boljim i sretnijim vremenima. Podsjeća na uzrečicu koju je često čula: **najsretnija je ona zemlja u kojoj građani ne znaju tko im je premijer, pa ni predsjednik**.

Otada se, ističe, dogodilo toliko turbulentnih zbivanja da su se svijet i međunarodni odnosi promijenili iz temelja. Kao glavne uzroke snažne politizacije društva navodi:

- **velike geopolitičke izazove** na koje vlade očito nisu pružile dobre odgovore,
- **veliko nezadovoljstvo građana** koje je iz toga proizašlo,
- **duboku polarizaciju društva**.

Posljedica je da se gotovo svaki izbori pretvaraju u referendum. Polović posebno ističe promjenu kod mladih. Sociolozi su godinama analizirali njihovu apolitičnost, a danas su mladi, prema njezinim riječima, „strahovito politički angažirani“. Za to su zaslužne i društvene mreže te alati kojima se politika predstavlja i u kojima građani mogu izravno sudjelovati. Zato danas vlada prava turbulencija izbora i događaja, a stvari se uglavnom vode **za i protiv političkih figura ili pokreta**.
sections.subtitle_en: When Every Election Becomes a Referendum: The End of the Era of Political Carefreeness
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović explains how turbulent events fundamentally changed the world and politicized citizens
sections.content_en:
The Radio Mrežnica podcast opens geopolitical topics once again. The host introduces the guest, **Jadranka Polović**, as one of the best geopolitical analysts in the region. Polović is a political scientist and research associate, and she earned her doctorate in the field of international relations, specifically on the topic of relations between the US and the region.

The conversation begins vividly. The host notes that not even the screenwriter of a turbulent geopolitical movie could conceive of the present that the world is currently living: elections in which both the small and the great fall, new wars that threaten, and old ones that do not end. She asks the guest to describe the times we live in through "women's geopolitical intuition."

Polović goes back two decades. At that time, she says, in a conversation like this, one could say that elections were not particularly important. People were not apolitical, but they lived in better and happier times. She recalls a saying she often heard: **the happiest country is the one where citizens do not know who their prime minister is, nor even the president**.

Since then, she points out, so many turbulent events have occurred that the world and international relations have changed fundamentally. As the main causes of the strong politicization of society, she cites:

- **major geopolitical challenges** to which governments clearly failed to provide good answers,
- **great citizen dissatisfaction** that resulted from this,
- **deep polarization of society**.

The consequence is that almost every election turns into a referendum. Polović particularly emphasizes the change among young people. Sociologists have analyzed their apolitical nature for years, but today young people, in her words, are "tremendously politically engaged." Social networks and the tools through which politics is presented and in which citizens can directly participate are also responsible for this. That is why today a real turbulence of elections and events prevails, and things are mostly waged **for and against political figures or movements**.

sections.subtitle: Midterm izbori kao presuda Trumpovoj politici
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava da su američki midterm izbori pretvoreni u referendum o Trumpovoj politici
sections.content:
Budući da je doktorirala na temi američke politike, voditeljica napominje da bi Polović „specijalnost“ mogao biti upravo Donald Trump. Pred njim su **midterm izbori**, pa pita hoće li se išta promijeniti.

Polović najprije podsjeća da su 2024. i 2025. bile godine „super izbora“. I ove je godine bilo više izbornih ciklusa, među kojima i izraelski izbori održani prije dva dana, čiji konačni rezultati još nisu poznati. Midterm izbori za Kongres, koji čine Zastupnički dom i Senat, ipak su vrlo važni. Kongres usvaja zakone i odlučuje o proračunu Sjedinjenih Američkih Država. U protekle dvije godine republikanci su imali većinu u oba doma, a sada su i ovi izbori pretvoreni u **referendum o politikama američkog predsjednika**.

Gošća naglašava da to nije novost. Od 1946. predsjednička stranka na midterm izborima u pravilu gubi. Polović iznosi brojku od otprilike 26,5 do 27, podatak koji je, kako kaže, provjerila tog jutra, i povezuje je s gubitkom mjesta u Zastupničkom domu. Uz to se obično izgubi i nekoliko mjesta u Senatu.

U slučaju Trumpa, prema njezinoj ocjeni, „naslagalo se jako puno“. Problematična pitanja za većinu američkih građana su:

- gospodarska situacija i **troškovi života**,
- visoka inflacija i visoke cijene,
- stanovanje i zdravstvena zaštita,
- **migracije**, oko kojih se „lome koplja“,
- demokracija i **povjerenje u institucije**.

Polović dodaje da su troškovi života u Americi i dalje povoljniji nego u Europi, ali Amerikanci, barem dio njih, vole udobno živjeti. Posebno ističe **rat u Iranu**. Riječ je o vanjskopolitičkom pitanju, ali je zbog rasta cijena energenata postao pitanje domaće politike.

Svi očekuju da će Trump izgubiti Zastupnički dom, dok je Senat neizvjestan. Ako omjer bude 50:50, presudni glas ima potpredsjednik **J. D. Vance**. Polović ipak upozorava da Trump vlada „vrlo opušteno“: služi se predsjedničkim uredbama i zaobilazi institucionalna ograničenja. Zato vjeruje da će učiniti sve kako bi nastavio svojim putem.

Predsjednici u posljednje dvije godine mandata obično dovršavaju započete poslove. Trump je, međutim, prema njezinim riječima, unatoč godinama „pun elana“ i otvorit će nove poslove, što može značiti i nove krize. Neke bi možda i uspio riješiti. Voditeljica zaključuje da je posao tek pred njim, a Polović se smijući slaže: „Život je pred njim.“
sections.subtitle_en: Midterm Elections as a Verdict on Trump's Policy
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that the US midterm elections have turned into a referendum on Trump's policy
sections.content_en:
Since she earned her doctorate on the topic of American politics, the host notes that Polović's "specialty" could be none other than Donald Trump. Ahead of him are the **midterm elections**, so she asks whether anything will change.

Polović first recalls that 2024 and 2025 were years of "super elections." This year, too, there were multiple election cycles, including the Israeli elections held two days ago, whose final results are not yet known. The midterm elections for Congress, which consists of the House of Representatives and the Senate, are nevertheless very important. Congress passes laws and decides on the budget of the United States of America. Over the past two years, Republicans held a majority in both chambers, and now these elections, too, have turned into a **referendum on the policies of the American president**.

The guest emphasizes that this is nothing new. Since 1946, the president's party as a rule loses in midterm elections. Polović presents a figure of roughly 26.5 to 27, data that she, as she says, checked that morning, and connects it with the loss of seats in the House of Representatives. In addition, several seats are usually lost in the Senate as well.

In Trump's case, according to her assessment, "a huge amount has piled up." Problematic issues for the majority of American citizens are:

- the economic situation and **costs of living**,
- high inflation and high prices,
- housing and healthcare,
- **migrations**, over which "spears are being broken,"
- democracy and **trust in institutions**.

Polović adds that the cost of living in America is still more affordable than in Europe, but Americans, at least a part of them, like to live comfortably. She particularly highlights the **war in Iran**. It is a foreign policy issue, but due to rising energy prices, it has become a domestic policy issue.

Everyone expects Trump to lose the House of Representatives, while the Senate is uncertain. If the ratio is 50:50, Vice President **J. D. Vance** holds the decisive vote. Polović nevertheless warns that Trump governs "very casually": he uses executive orders and bypasses institutional limitations. That is why she believes he will do everything to continue on his path.

Presidents in the last two years of their term usually finish things they have started. Trump, however, in her words, despite his age is "full of drive" and will open up new projects, which may also mean new crises. Some he might even manage to resolve. The host concludes that the work is only ahead of him, and Polović agrees with a laugh: "Life is ahead of him."

sections.subtitle: Iran pred novim udarom: rat bez ostvarenih ciljeva
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović tumači zašto američka administracija u Iranu nije ostvarila nijedan cilj
sections.content:
Na pitanje bi li Trump mogao ponovno napasti Iran, Polović odgovara da „to svi očekuju“. Voditeljica podsjeća na upozorenje koje je SAD uputio partnerima. Gošća dodaje da je signal jasan: kada američka vlada povlači diplomate i njihove obitelji, „onda znate da neće biti dobro“.

Rat u Iranu, ocjenjuje Polović, Trumpa je zapravo učinio gubitnikom, ali on to nikada neće pokazati. Trump je pragmatičan, poslovan čovjek i takav mentalni sklop primjenjuje i na politiku. **Američka administracija u Iranu nije ostvarila nijedan cilj.** Trump je cijelo vrijeme poručivao da su pregovori samo što nisu počeli i da će uskoro biti postignut „najbolji sporazum na svijetu“. U međuvremenu je Hormuz otvoren, ali je zatvoren **Bab el-Mandeb**.

Voditeljica se pritom prisjeća Trumpove retorike o „majci svih bombi“. Polović podsjeća da je u regiju poslan i treći nosač zrakoplova, **Theodore Roosevelt**, pa je koncentracija vojnih snaga velika. Otvoreno je pitanje što se može postići „jednim beskrajnim razaranjem“.

Iran je, kaže gošća, „vrlo tvrd orah“, ali nije nepobjediv. Na početku se računalo na **obojenu revoluciju** i promjenu režima iznutra, igrom na Kurde, Beludže i druge manjinske skupine. Dogodilo se suprotno: Iranci su, iz straha ili iz rodoljublja, zbili redove. Polović kao čudnu činjenicu navodi da Iran uživa određenu podršku i u zapadnom svijetu. Politika otpora, odnosno **„osovine otpora“** i njezinih saveznika, pokazala se iznimno uspješnom, što se vidi i na primjeru Huta.

Trump ipak ne odustaje. Polović smatra da on uopće ne percipira vrijeme. Ako procijeni da zbog Irana gubi na domaćem terenu, usporit će, ali neće zaboraviti. Podsjeća da je već u prvom mandatu radio sve kako bi odustao od nuklearnog sporazuma, koji ocjenjuje kao dobar i prihvatljiv. Legitimno je pitanje, kaže, radi li to samoinicijativno ili pod utjecajem izraelske vlade, prvenstveno **Netanyahua**. U svakom slučaju, Trump prema toj temi pokazuje „veliku strast“.

Polović očekuje barem nekoliko velikih napada na Iran, ali napominje da su Iranci spremni. Voditeljica zaključuje da bi ishod opet mogao biti neriješen, s čime se gošća slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Iran Facing a New Strike: A War Without Achieved Goals
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović explains why the US administration in Iran has not achieved a single goal
sections.content_en:
When asked whether Trump could attack Iran again, Polović replies that "everyone expects that." The host recalls the warning that the US issued to partners. The guest adds that the signal is clear: when the American government withdraws diplomats and their families, "then you know it won't be good."

The war in Iran, Polović assesses, has actually made Trump a loser, but he will never show it. Trump is a pragmatic, business-minded man, and he applies that mindset to politics as well. **The American administration in Iran has not achieved a single goal.** Trump was saying all along that negotiations were just about to begin and that "the best deal in the world" would soon be reached. Meanwhile, Hormuz is open, but **Bab el-Mandeb** is closed.

The host recalls Trump's rhetoric about the "mother of all bombs." Polović recalls that a third aircraft carrier, the **Theodore Roosevelt**, was also sent to the region, so the concentration of military forces is high. The question of what can be achieved by "one endless destruction" remains open.

Iran is, says the guest, "a very tough nut to crack," but it is not invincible. At the beginning, a **color revolution** and regime change from within were counted on, playing on the Kurds, Balochs, and other minority groups. The opposite occurred: Iranians, out of fear or out of patriotism, closed ranks. Polović mentions as a strange fact that Iran enjoys certain support in the Western world as well. The policy of resistance, that is, the **"axis of resistance"** and its allies, proved to be exceptionally successful, which is also seen in the example of the Houthis.

Trump, however, does not give up. Polović believes that he does not perceive time at all. If he judges that he is losing on the domestic front because of Iran, he will slow down, but he will not forget. She recalls that already during his first term he did everything to abandon the nuclear agreement, which she assesses as good and acceptable. It is a legitimate question, she says, whether he does that on his own initiative or under the influence of the Israeli government, primarily **Netanyahu**. In any case, Trump shows "great passion" toward that topic.

Polović expects at least a few major strikes on Iran, but notes that the Iranians are ready. The host concludes that the outcome could again be a draw, with which the guest agrees.

sections.subtitle: Izrael nakon izbora: nova matematika, ista politika
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća iznosi preliminarne brojke mandata Netanyahuova i oporbenog bloka
sections.content:
Voditeljica primjećuje da je Netanyahu na izraelskim izborima „dobio, a zapravo nije dobio“. Pita bi li se u odnosu Izraela i njegova najvećeg prijatelja, Amerike, odnosno Donalda Trumpa, išta moglo promijeniti. Polović odgovara kratko: „Ništa novo pod suncem.“

Kao ilustraciju navodi istraživanje među mladim biračima koji su prvi put izašli na izbore. Prema njemu se **dvije trećine deklarira kao tvrdi desničari**, što znači da podržavaju Likud i Netanyahuovu vladu. I oporbeni, anti-Netanyahuov blok sastavljen od različitih političkih opcija ima svoje jastrebove, a među njegovim predvodnicima je bivši izraelski premijer **Bennett**. Zato, zaključuje, nema promjene politike ni prema Gazi, ni prema Iranu, ni prema ostalim zemljama regije.

Polović ipak vidi mogućnost da bi dolazak oporbenog bloka donekle smirio tenzije i otvorio prostor za diplomaciju. Rezultate je pregledala tog jutra. Preliminarni će biti objavljeni sutradan, a službeni za tjedan dana. Trenutačno stanje izgleda ovako:

- **Likud** je pojedinačno najjača stranka,
- **Netanyahuov blok** ima 53 mandata, a za većinu mu treba 61,
- **anti-Netanyahuov blok** ima 48 mandata,
- prevagu bi mogle donijeti **dvije arapske stranke**, koje, kako dobacuje voditeljica, upravo nitko ne želi.

Gošća upozorava da su teme koje se lome u Izraelu manje vidljive u Europi. Najveća je polemika oko **7. listopada 2023.**: je li Netanyahu znao za napad i jesu li obavještajna zajednica, vojska i cijeli sustav reagirali primjereno. Prema Polović, sada je posve jasno da su obavještajni podaci postojali i bili ignorirani. Postavlja se pitanje zašto i tko ih je ignorirao.

Korupcijske procese protiv Netanyahua smatra nevažnima, jer su ljudi, kaže, već zaboravili zbog čega je uopće optužen. Mnogo osjetljivijim smatra njegovu odluku da **ultraortodoksne Židove oslobodi služenja vojnog roka**, što u Izraelu izaziva velike polemike. Podrška politici prema Gazi i Iranu, ratu općenito te **projektu „velikog Izraela“** ostaje, prema njezinoj ocjeni, na dnevnom redu bez obzira na to koja opcija dođe na vlast. Voditeljica zaključuje da se samo čeka druga konstelacija odnosa, a Polović se slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Israel After the Elections: New Mathematics, Same Policy
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest presents preliminary mandate figures for Netanyahu's and the opposition bloc
sections.content_en:
The host observes that Netanyahu, in the Israeli elections, "won, but actually didn't win." She asks whether anything could change in the relationship between Israel and its greatest friend, America, namely Donald Trump. Polović answers briefly: "Nothing new under the sun."

As an illustration, she cites research among young voters who cast their ballots for the first time. According to it, **two-thirds declare themselves as hard right-wingers**, which means they support Likud and Netanyahu's government. The opposition, anti-Netanyahu bloc composed of various political options also has its hawks, and among its leaders is former Israeli prime minister **Bennett**. Therefore, she concludes, there is no change in policy toward Gaza, toward Iran, or toward the other countries of the region.

Polović nevertheless sees the possibility that the arrival of the opposition bloc might somewhat calm tensions and open space for diplomacy. She reviewed the results that morning. Preliminary ones will be published the following day, and official ones in a week. The current state of affairs looks like this:

- **Likud** is individually the strongest party,
- **Netanyahu's bloc** has 53 mandates, and needs 61 for a majority,
- the **anti-Netanyahu bloc** has 48 mandates,
- the tipping point could be brought by **two Arab parties**, which, as the host interjects, practically no one wants.

The guest warns that the issues dividing Israel are less visible in Europe. The biggest controversy is around **October 7, 2023**: did Netanyahu know about the attack and did the intelligence community, the army, and the whole system react appropriately. According to Polović, it is now entirely clear that intelligence data existed and was ignored. The question arises why and who ignored it.

She considers the corruption trials against Netanyahu unimportant, because people, she says, have already forgotten what he was even accused of. She considers much more sensitive his decision to **exempt ultra-Orthodox Jews from military service**, which causes great controversies in Israel. Support for policy toward Gaza and Iran, for the war in general, and for the **"Greater Israel" project** remains, in her assessment, on the agenda regardless of which option comes to power. The host concludes that they are merely waiting for a different constellation of relations, and Polović agrees.

sections.subtitle: Iran za Ukrajinu? Velika trojka i crtanje nove karte svijeta
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović govori o sastanku Trumpa, Putina i Šija i podjeli sfera utjecaja
sections.content:
Voditeljica uz igru riječi postavlja pitanje je li moguće da Trump „trampi“ Iran za Ukrajinu. Zamišlja dogovor u novostvorenim odnosima Rusije i SAD-a: Trump bi Putinu poručio da smiri Irance dok ih on „malo izbombardira“, a zauzvrat bi mu riješio Ukrajinu. Polović ocjenjuje da je to „vrlo lako moguće“. Prvi razlog vidi u pripremi velikog sastanka trojice lidera: **Trumpa, Putina i Šija**. Oni bi razmatrali globalna pitanja ili, kako dodaje voditeljica, „crtali novu kartu svijeta“.

Trumpu je, prema gošći, iznimno važna nuklearna tema, jer su istekli svi sporazumi o nuklearnom naoružanju i zaštiti od njega. Polović upozorava da ljudi toga nisu svjesni: svijet je danas **bez ikakvih međunarodnih sporazuma** i prepušten je savjesti i pameti svjetskih lidera. Putin ima druge namjere, jer je Rusija velika nuklearna sila, a Ši ima vlastitu problematiku. Kako god sastanak izgledao, moguća je **podjela sfera interesa i utjecaja**.

Iran bi, smatra Polović, prije mogao dobiti podršku Kine nego Rusije. Ipak upozorava da je na djelu „velika igra“. Trump se odvaja od Ukrajine, ali joj i dalje šalje oružje koje plaća Europska unija. U svemu tome ima mnogo „prljave igre“ koju je iz ove perspektive teško shvatiti.

Gošća zatim širi kut gledanja. Svijet prolazi kroz turbulencije svjetskog poretka, od **unipolarnog sustava** u kojem su SAD dominirale uz podršku gotovo svih, pa i Rusije i Kine, prema svijetu **bez globalnog vodstva**:

- **Kina** bi ekonomski možda mogla preuzeti tu ulogu i razvija vojsku, ali prema ocjeni Polović uopće nije zainteresirana za poziciju globalnog lidera,
- **Rusija** ima oružje, ali nema snagu ni kapacitet „države-civilizacije“ koja bi vodila svijet,
- **SAD** se u preustroju međunarodnog poretka ponašaju „kao slon u staklani“.

Zato treba očekivati mnogo novih ratova i sukoba. Polović naglašava da to nisu procesi od jednog desetljeća nakon kojeg slijedi mir, nego procesi koji traju **sto i više godina**. Kao usporedbu navodi raspad Rimskog Carstva, tijekom kojeg su prošle brojne generacije.
sections.subtitle_en: Iran for Ukraine? The Big Three and Drawing a New Map of the World
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović speaks about the meeting between Trump, Putin, and Xi and the division of spheres of influence
sections.content_en:
The host, using a play on words, poses the question of whether it is possible that Trump will "trade" Iran for Ukraine. She imagines an agreement in the newly created relations between Russia and the US: Trump would tell Putin to calm the Iranians down while he "bombs them a little bit," and in return would settle Ukraine for him. Polović assesses that this is "very easily possible." She sees the first reason in the preparation of a major meeting of three leaders: **Trump, Putin, and Xi**. They would consider global issues or, as the host adds, "draw a new map of the world."

For Trump, according to the guest, the nuclear topic is exceptionally important, because all agreements on nuclear weapons and protection from them have expired. Polović warns that people are not aware of this: the world today is **without any international agreements** and is left to the conscience and intellect of world leaders. Putin has other intentions, because Russia is a major nuclear power, and Xi has his own set of issues. However the meeting looks, a **division of spheres of interest and influence** is possible.

Iran, Polović believes, could sooner receive support from China than from Russia. Yet she warns that a "great game" is underway. Trump is detaching himself from Ukraine, but still sends it weapons paid for by the European Union. In all of this there is a lot of "dirty game" that is difficult to understand from this perspective.

The guest then widens the angle of view. The world is going through turbulences of the world order, from a **unipolar system** in which the US dominated with the support of almost everyone, including Russia and China, toward a world **without global leadership**:

- **China** could perhaps economically take over that role and is developing its military, but according to Polović's assessment is not at all interested in the position of global leader,
- **Russia** has weapons, but lacks the strength and capacity of a "civilization-state" that would lead the world,
- the **US** behaves "like a bull in a china shop" in the restructuring of the international order.

Therefore, one should expect many new wars and conflicts. Polović emphasizes that these are not processes of a single decade followed by peace, but processes lasting **one hundred years and more**. As a comparison, she cites the collapse of the Roman Empire, during which numerous generations passed.

sections.subtitle: Crveni tepisi, večere i sjena ratova: diplomatski glamur i zaboravljeni Kim
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća se čudi što na sastanak velike trojke nije pozvan sjevernokorejski vođa Kim
sections.content:
Voditeljica pita tko bi na još nepotvrđenom sastanku velike trojke bio „najgizdaviji“ i napominje da je čitala tekstove prema kojima Trumpu imponira društvo najjačih. Polović potvrđuje da se to vidi. Trump je kineskom i ruskom predsjedniku iskazao **veliku diplomatsku počast** i prostro crvene tepihe. Nije uobičajeno da osobno dočeka drugog državnika na aerodromu, ali Šija je dočekao, i to s Melanijom. Priredio je i večere, što Polović opisuje kao „nevjerojatan diplomatski prijem“. „Oni to pamte“, dodaje.

Iza glamura ona vidi ozbiljniju sliku. Sve je to „jako lijepo, baš kulturno, baš su džentlmeni“, ali nad sastankom ostaje **sjena ratova i smrti** u sukobima koje su ti akteri proizveli i izazvali. Na stolu su, naglašava, vrlo ozbiljna i značajna pitanja. Dodaje i da su Ši i Putin „pročitali Trumpa“: znaju da jedan dan kaže jedno, a drugi dan se predomisli, ali da je prema njima „slatkorječiv“.

Gošću čudi što na sastanak nije pozvan i **sjevernokorejski Kim**. Kaže da je „malo pomaknut“, ali ima nuklearno oružje i ušao je u prvu četvorku ili petorku nuklearnih sila. Voditeljica dobacuje da „nije za zezanje“, a Polović se slaže. Podsjeća na Trumpov prvi mandat, kada je Trump „navalio“ na Sjevernu Koreju. Kim je tada ispalio dva-tri projektila prema američkoj bazi **Guam** u Pacifiku, a zatim prema Japanu. Nakon toga je Trump otišao k njemu i, kako kaže, „poklonio se“. Postali su „frendovi“ i priča je zasad završena.

Polović dodaje da Kim danas reklamira Sjevernu Koreju na Instagramu. Ulazak još nije dopušten svima, ali u zemlju ulazi mnogo ruskih turista, a dostupne su i snimke. Ipak upozorava da Trump Kima nije zaboravio i da bi se u nekom trenutku tu mogao otvoriti novi problem. Voditeljica na kraju povezuje dvije slike: ruski turisti u Sjevernoj Koreji i sjevernokorejski vojnici na ukrajinskom ratištu.
sections.subtitle_en: Red Carpets, Dinners, and the Shadow of Wars: Diplomatic Glamour and the Forgotten Kim
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest finds it surprising that North Korean leader Kim was not invited to the meeting of the Big Three
sections.content_en:
The host asks who would be the "most dashing" at the yet-unconfirmed meeting of the Big Three and notes that she read articles according to which Trump is impressed by the company of the strongest. Polović confirms that this can be seen. Trump showed **great diplomatic honor** to the Chinese and Russian presidents and rolled out red carpets. It is not customary for him to personally welcome another statesman at the airport, but he welcomed Xi, and with Melania. He also arranged dinners, which Polović describes as an "incredible diplomatic reception." "They remember that," she adds.

Behind the glamour she sees a more serious picture. All of that is "very nice, truly refined, they are real gentlemen," but over the meeting remains the **shadow of wars and death** in conflicts that these actors produced and caused. On the table, she emphasizes, are very serious and significant issues. She also adds that Xi and Putin have "read Trump": they know that one day he says one thing, and the next day changes his mind, but that toward them he is "smooth-talking."

The guest finds it surprising that **North Korea's Kim** was not invited to the meeting as well. She says that he is "a bit eccentric," but he has nuclear weapons and has entered the top four or five nuclear powers. The host interjects that he is "not one to be trifled with," and Polović agrees. She recalls Trump's first term, when Trump "went all out" against North Korea. Kim then fired two or three missiles toward the American base **Guam** in the Pacific, and then toward Japan. After that, Trump went to him and, as she says, "bowed." They became "friends" and the story is finished for now.

Polović adds that Kim today advertises North Korea on Instagram. Entry is not yet permitted to everyone, but many Russian tourists enter the country, and footage is available. Nevertheless, she warns that Trump has not forgotten Kim and that at some point a new problem could open up there. The host finally connects two images: Russian tourists in North Korea and North Korean soldiers on the Ukrainian battlefield.

sections.subtitle: Abu Dhabi i put prema miru: neutralna Ukrajina i nedjeljiva europska sigurnost
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović iznosi preduvjete za završetak rata: neutralnost Ukrajine i odustajanje od NATO-a
sections.content:
Razgovor prelazi na Ukrajinu. Voditeljica podsjeća na najavljeni, još nepotvrđeni **tripartitni sastanak** predstavnika Rusije, Ukrajine i SAD-a u Abu Dhabiju, koji bi se trebao održati u prvih deset dana studenog. Pita hoće li se tamo „dogovoriti Ukrajina“.

Polović Ukrajinu opisuje kao veliko otvoreno europsko pitanje. Rat traje četiri i pol godine i odnio je nevjerojatan broj žrtava, a spekulira se i o **dva milijuna ljudi**. Tome treba dodati raseljene i uništene živote. Rat zato mora završiti. **Trumpovu inicijativu** i pritisak koji vrši na čelnike Europske unije i na predsjednika Zelenskog smatra ispravnima, jer se treba vratiti diplomaciji.

Kritična je prema Europi, koja je prema njezinim riječima od početka postigla **konsenzus o bojkotu diplomacije**. Ukrajina, kaže, nije trebala izgubiti toliko teritorija. Prilike su postojale u Minskim sporazumima, a kasnije i na pregovorima u Turskoj, za koje se ne sjeća točno jesu li bili 2022. ili 2023. Tada još nije bilo izgubljeno toliko teritorija.

Gošća spominje da je nedavno ponovno pročitala tekstove koje je napisala na početku sukoba. Nije predlagala gotova rješenja, nego je analizirala kako se rat može zaustaviti. Tada su joj bila jasna dva preduvjeta:

- **NATO treba napustiti Ukrajinu**,
- **Ukrajina treba biti neutralna država**, što je preduvjet za rješavanje ostalih otvorenih pitanja.

Uz ranije ruske zahtjeve o demilitarizaciji i denacifikaciji danas se pojavio i zahtjev za **sigurnosnim jamstvima ne samo Ukrajini nego i Rusiji**. To znači da Rusija traži da bude uključena. Polović podsjeća da je Rusija dijelom europska zemlja i da se na zajedničkom kontinentu ne može pobjeći jedni od drugih. Uz ironičan komentar o ponovnom podizanju „onog berlinskog zida“ zalaže se za povratak konceptu **nedjeljive europske sigurnosti**, proizašlom iz završnog akta Konferencije o europskoj sigurnosti i suradnji iz 20. stoljeća. To je, kaže, bilo „najnormalnije riješeno“ i ne može razumjeti zašto je sve otišlo u krivom smjeru. Poziva na povratak normalnim postavkama i diplomaciji kako bi se sukob okončao.
entities: Konferencija o europskoj sigurnosti i suradnji
sections.subtitle_en: Abu Dhabi and the Path Toward Peace: Neutral Ukraine and Indivisible European Security
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović outlines preconditions for ending the war: neutrality of Ukraine and giving up on NATO
sections.content_en:
The conversation moves on to Ukraine. The host recalls the announced, yet-unconfirmed **tripartite meeting** of representatives of Russia, Ukraine, and the US in Abu Dhabi, which should take place in the first ten days of November. She asks whether "Ukraine will be agreed upon" there.

Polović describes Ukraine as a major unresolved European issue. The war has lasted four and a half years and has claimed an incredible number of casualties, with speculation even reaching **two million people**. To that should be added displaced persons and ruined lives. The war therefore must end. She considers **Trump's initiative** and the pressure he exerts on European Union leaders and on President Zelenskyy to be correct, because one must return to diplomacy.

She is critical of Europe, which according to her words achieved a **consensus on boycotting diplomacy** from the beginning. Ukraine, she says, should not have lost so much territory. Opportunities existed in the Minsk agreements, and later in the negotiations in Turkey, for which she does not remember exactly whether they were in 2022 or 2023. At that time so much territory had not yet been lost.

The guest mentions that she recently re-read texts she wrote at the beginning of the conflict. She did not propose ready-made solutions, but analyzed how the war could be stopped. At that time, two preconditions were clear to her:

- **NATO needs to leave Ukraine**,
- **Ukraine needs to be a neutral state**, which is a precondition for resolving the other open issues.

Along with earlier Russian demands for demilitarization and denazification, today a demand for **security guarantees not only for Ukraine but also for Russia** has also emerged. This means that Russia is demanding to be included. Polović recalls that Russia is partly a European country and that on a shared continent one cannot escape from one another. With an ironic comment about re-erecting "that Berlin Wall," she advocates a return to the concept of **indivisible European security**, stemming from the final act of the Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe from the 20th century. That, she says, was "resolved most normally" and she cannot understand why everything went in the wrong direction. She calls for a return to normal baseline settings and diplomacy in order to end the conflict.

sections.subtitle: „Koji je broj Europe?“ Nordijski pozivi Putinu i potraga za pregovaračem
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća s nevjericom komentira kako Europa traži osobu koja bi pregovarala s Putinom
sections.content:
Voditeljica otvara temu nedavnih telefonskih razgovora dvojice nordijskih čelnika s Putinom, među kojima spominje Stubba. Razgovore su potvrdile obje strane. Nazvani su se ubrzo ogradili da ne nastupaju u ime Europe, koja mora biti jedinstvena. Voditeljica pita je li to početak nove diplomacije, omekšavanje ili pokušaj da se Putina slomi. Podsjeća i da je u Moskvi nedavno bio šef CIA-e, kojega Putin nije primio, te da je Putin vjerojatno stalno na vezi s Trumpom.

Polović vjeruje da je pomak moguć, ali Putin ostaje pri svojim zahtjevima i od njih „uopće ne odstupa“. Istodobno poziva Europljane za stol. Najnovija poruka iz Kremlja ipak je da Europljani ne mogu sjediti za stolom u Abu Dhabiju.

Gošća ne skriva nevjericu nad europskim pristupom. Europa, kaže, kao da „natječajem traži“ ili „iz šešira vuče“ osobu koja će pregovarati s Putinom, što smatra potpuno smiješnim. Po hijerarhiji bi to trebala biti **predsjednica Europske komisije**, koja bi se s Putinom našla na neutralnom teritoriju i objasnila europske pozicije, dok bi on objasnio ruske. Suglasja o tome nema, a Polović podsjeća na Kissingerovu izjavu. Kada su mu rekli da razgovara s Europom, upitao je: **„Koji je broj Europe?“** „I to je zaista tako“, zaključuje.

Nordijske čelnike vidi u drukčijem svjetlu. Nazvali su samoinicijativno, ne u ime Europe, jer su shvatili da **ističe vrijeme**. Situacija na Baltiku, osobito oko **Kalinjingrada**, iznimno se komplicira. Na terenu je s obje strane prisutna velika količina nuklearnog oružja, uključujući famozni **Orešnik** u Bjelorusiji. Čelnici zemalja blizu Rusije htjeli su objasniti poziciju svojih država i smiriti situaciju. „To bi napravio svaki odgovorni državnik, jer mu je to u opisu posla“, ističe Polović.

Osvrće se i na napis Timesa prema kojem je Putin sugovornicima sat i pol držao lekcije o prošlosti, što je Kremlj demantirao. Voditeljica primjećuje da ne treba sve vjerovati, a gošća se slaže. Smatra da je razgovor bio ravnopravan i da je Putin ostavio prostor za nastavak. Prema objavi na stranicama ministarstva, mogu ga nazvati kad god imaju potrebu. Dijalog se, zaključuje Polović, mora pokrenuti.
sections.subtitle_en: "What Is Europe's Number?" Nordic Calls to Putin and the Search for a Negotiator
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest comments with disbelief on how Europe is searching for a person to negotiate with Putin
sections.content_en:
The host opens the topic of recent telephone conversations between two Nordic leaders and Putin, mentioning Stubb among them. The conversations were confirmed by both sides. Those called soon qualified that they do not act on behalf of Europe, which must be unified. The host asks whether this is the beginning of a new diplomacy, a softening, or an attempt to break Putin. She also recalls that the head of the CIA was recently in Moscow, whom Putin did not receive, and that Putin is probably constantly in touch with Trump.

Polović believes progress is possible, but Putin stands by his demands and from them "does not deviate at all." At the same time, he invites Europeans to the table. The latest message from the Kremlin, however, is that Europeans cannot sit at the table in Abu Dhabi.

The guest does not hide her disbelief at the European approach. Europe, she says, seems to be "searching via tender" or "pulling out of a hat" a person who will negotiate with Putin, which she considers completely ridiculous. By hierarchy that should be the **President of the European Commission**, who would meet with Putin on neutral territory and explain European positions, while he would explain Russian ones. There is no consensus on this, and Polović recalls Kissinger's statement. When they told him to speak with Europe, he asked: **"What is Europe's number?"** "And that is truly so," she concludes.

She sees Nordic leaders in a different light. They called on their own initiative, not on behalf of Europe, because they realized that **time is running out**. The situation in the Baltic, especially around **Kaliningrad**, is becoming extremely complicated. On the ground, a large quantity of nuclear weapons is present on both sides, including the infamous **Oreshnik** in Belarus. Leaders of countries near Russia wanted to explain the position of their states and calm the situation. "Every responsible statesman would do that, because that is in his job description," Polović points out.

She also reflects on a Times article according to which Putin lectured his interlocutors about the past for an hour and a half, which the Kremlin denied. The host observes that one shouldn't believe everything, and the guest agrees. She believes the conversation was on equal footing and that Putin left room for continuation. According to the announcement on the ministry's website, they can call him whenever they feel the need. Dialogue, Polović concludes, must be initiated.

sections.subtitle: Pregovarati s neprijateljem nije izdaja: od Tuđmana i Miloševića do sankcija koje su pogodile Europu
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović objašnjava kako su sankcije pogoršale europsko gospodarstvo, a ojačale rusko
sections.content:
Polović kritizira klimu u kojoj svatko tko spomene Putina ili kaže da bi s njim razgovarao dobiva etiketu **„rusofila“**, osobe koja promiče rusku politiku. To smatra „potpuno suludim“ i neistinitim. Voditeljica povlači paralelu s Hrvatskom: sugovornici podcasta često podsjećaju da je Hrvatska bila u ratu sa Srbijom, a ipak se pregovaralo. Jesu li hrvatski pregovarači tada bili „srbofili“? Polović odgovara odrično i podsjeća na **sastanke Tuđmana i Miloševića**. Linije, kaže, moraju ostati otvorene i, ako treba, mora se sastati.

Na pitanje odakle tolika europska tvrdoća, gošća slikovito kaže da Europljani „skaču kao muhe po slonu“. Rusija je ogromna država i nuklearna sila. Godinama se ponavljala parola da se rat vodi do pobjede nad Rusijom, što se, prema njezinoj ocjeni, praktički neće dogoditi. Iza te ideje vidi želju za **povratkom u devedesete**, kada bi ruski resursi postali dostupni europskim i svjetskim korporacijama. Voditeljica pita misli li pritom na komadanje Rusije, a Polović potvrđuje. Naglašava da to „nisu teorije zavjere“ i da o tome postoje konkretni dokumenti i rasprave. Ta su vremena, dodaje, prošla.

Posebno se osvrće na sankcije. Prema njezinim riječima, Europa je njima **sama sebi pogoršala gospodarsku situaciju**. Na ruskoj strani dogodio se zaokret upravo u trenutku uvođenja sankcija i blokade privatne i državne ruske imovine u inozemstvu:

- ruski oligarsi i bogataši počeli su **ulagati u Rusiji**,
- rusko gospodarstvo se time podiglo,
- razvila se i **vojna industrija**,
- Rusija, prema ocjeni Polović, „nikad nije bolje stajala“.

Zaključuje da rat ni Rusiju zapravo ne zanima, jer je postao **biznis**, i to ne samo ruski nego i europskih zemalja.
sections.subtitle_en: Negotiating with the Enemy Is Not Treason: From Tuđman and Milošević to Sanctions That Hit Europe
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović explains how sanctions worsened the European economy while strengthening the Russian one
sections.content_en:
Polović criticizes the atmosphere in which anyone who mentions Putin or says they would talk with him gets the label of **"Russophile"**, a person who promotes Russian policy. She considers this "completely insane" and untrue. The host draws a parallel with Croatia: guests on the podcast often recall that Croatia was at war with Serbia, yet they negotiated. Were Croatian negotiators back then "Serbophiles"? Polović answers in the negative and recalls the **meetings of Tuđman and Milošević**. Lines, she says, must remain open and, if necessary, one must meet.

To the question of where such European rigidity comes from, the guest vividly says that Europeans "jump like flies on an elephant." Russia is a huge state and a nuclear power. For years, the slogan was repeated that the war is waged until victory over Russia, which, according to her assessment, practically will not happen. Behind that idea she sees a desire to **return to the nineties**, when Russian resources would become accessible to European and global corporations. The host asks if she means the dismemberment of Russia by that, and Polović confirms. She emphasizes that these "are not conspiracy theories" and that concrete documents and debates exist about it. Those times, she adds, have passed.

She particularly reflects on sanctions. According to her words, Europe with them **worsened its own economic situation**. On the Russian side, a turnaround occurred precisely at the moment of introducing sanctions and freezing private and state Russian assets abroad:

- Russian oligarchs and wealthy individuals began to **invest in Russia**,
- the Russian economy picked up as a result,
- the **military industry** also developed,
- Russia, according to Polović's assessment, "has never been better off."

She concludes that Russia is not really interested in the war either, because it has become a **business**, not only Russian but also of European countries.

sections.subtitle: Europa izvan stola: najveći financijer bez pravog glasa
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća podsjeća na Putinov zahtjev za sigurnosnim jamstvima iz prosinca 2021. upućen SAD-u i NATO-u, ali ne i EU-u
sections.content:
Voditeljica se ironično osvrće na godinama ponavljane tvrdnje da je Rusija pred propašću, uz priče o „veš-mašinama i čipovima“, te konstatira da je Europa iz pregovora „otpiljena“. Polović se slaže da bi Europa kao najveći financijer Ukrajine trebala sjediti za stolom. Riječ je o europskom pitanju i Europa bi trebala biti najzainteresiranija za smirivanje rata i primjenu diplomacije.

Europska unija, podsjeća gošća, nema vojnu silu, ali je uvijek imala **soft power**: diplomatsko pregovaranje, trgovinska rješenja i ljudska prava. Imala je i snažnu **privlačnost europeizacije**, koja je privlačila ne samo zemlje članice i kandidatkinje nego i samu Rusiju. Rusija je danas okrenuta istoku i surađuje s Indijom, Kinom i drugima, ali bi se, prema njezinoj ocjeni, vrlo lako vratila na zapad. Kao primjer navodi brzo postignut dizelski sporazum s Trumpom, nakon kojeg su već krenuli prvi tankeri.

U Rusiji postoje dvije struje, one okrenute zapadu i one okrenute istoku. Polović ističe da je ruska geopolitička misao vrlo razvijena, iako se o njoj u nas malo zna. Spominje **Dugina i Karaganova** kao teoretičare koji zagovaraju potpuno odvajanje od Europe i okretanje istoku. Ipak smatra da **Rusija bez Europe ne može biti imperijalna sila**. Ne misli pritom na napad ili osvajanje teritorija, jer Rusija ima golema nenaseljena područja koja su joj problem. Misli na veze kakve su postojale nakon Hladnog rata, koje bi ondje bile dobrodošle.

Voditeljica spominje izjavu **Ušakova** da Europljani mogu doći na sastanak u Abu Dhabiju „ako kupe kartu“ i ocjenjuje je kao stav „s visoka“. Polović napominje da sastanak još nije potvrđen. Voditeljica dodaje da bi ga situacija s Iranom mogla zakomplicirati ili odgoditi. Prema gošći, to bi bio prvi u nizu sastanaka, na razini **ekspertnih skupina**, odnosno tehnički dogovor o ključnim postavkama. Europljani su isključeni jer su postali izravna strana: i dalje financiraju te logistički i vojno pomažu Ukrajinu. Amerika se od rata distancirala, a Europa je, kaže, ostala „praktički stranka u ratu“.

Polović ipak dodaje važnu nijansu. U **prosincu 2021.** Putin je zahtjev za sigurnosnim jamstvima uputio SAD-u i NATO-u, ali ne Europskoj uniji. Time ju je sam izostavio od početka, no ni Europska unija se, naglašava, nije trudila uspostaviti bilo kakav kontakt s njim.
sections.subtitle_en: Europe Away From the Table: The Biggest Financier Without a Real Voice
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recalls Putin's demand for security guarantees from December 2021 addressed to the US and NATO, but not to the EU
sections.content_en:
The host ironically reflects on claims repeated for years that Russia was on the verge of collapse, along with stories about "washing machines and chips," and states that Europe has been "sawn off" from the negotiations. Polović agrees that Europe, as the biggest financier of Ukraine, should sit at the table. It is a European issue and Europe should be the most interested in calming the war and applying diplomacy.

The European Union, the guest recalls, does not have military power, but has always had **soft power**: diplomatic negotiation, trade solutions, and human rights. It also had the strong **appeal of Europeanization**, which attracted not only member states and candidates, but also Russia itself. Russia today is turned toward the East and cooperates with India, China, and others, but would, in her assessment, very easily return to the West. As an example, she cites the quickly reached diesel agreement with Trump, after which the first tankers already set sail.

In Russia there are two currents, those turned toward the West and those turned toward the East. Polović emphasizes that Russian geopolitical thought is very developed, although little is known about it among us. She mentions **Dugin and Karaganov** as theorists advocating complete detachment from Europe and turning toward the East. Nevertheless, she believes that **Russia cannot be an imperial power without Europe**. She does not mean attacking or conquering territory by that, because Russia has vast uninhabited areas that are a problem for it. She means ties like those that existed after the Cold War, which would be welcome there.

The host mentions the statement by **Ushakov** that Europeans can come to the meeting in Abu Dhabi "if they buy a ticket" and assesses it as a "condescending" stance. Polović notes that the meeting is not yet confirmed. The host adds that the situation with Iran could complicate or postpone it. According to the guest, this would be the first in a series of meetings, at the level of **expert groups**, that is, a technical agreement on key settings. Europeans are excluded because they have become a direct party: they continue to finance and provide logistical and military aid to Ukraine. America has distanced itself from the war, and Europe, she says, has remained "practically a party to the war."

Polović nevertheless adds an important nuance. In **December 2021**, Putin addressed the request for security guarantees to the US and NATO, but not to the European Union. By doing so, he left it out himself from the beginning, but the European Union, she emphasizes, made no effort to establish any kind of contact with him either.

sections.subtitle: Zelenski u Moskvi? Predsjednik koji gubi podršku na svim stranama
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović govori o gubitku podrške ukrajinskom predsjedniku kod kuće, u Americi i Europi
sections.content:
Voditeljica pita je li moguć odlazak **Zelenskog** u Moskvu, uz napomenu da neki tvrde kako on, zbog izostanka izbora, više i nije predsjednik. Pita i bi li to bio dobar PR, uz poziv u stilu „dođi, bit ćeš na sigurnom“. Polović uz smijeh kaže da bi to bila njezina „pitanja na koja se puno pita“. Osobno, kaže, ne bi otišla.

Obrazlaže to „vrlo čudnim stvarima“ koje se događaju na zapadu, gdje Amerika „otme predsjednika“. Voditeljica primjećuje da je zapad „postao divlji“. Polović dodaje da diplomatski imunitet na zapadu, kako se pokazalo, nije zajamčen onima koje se proglašava diktatorima. Kada bi jamstvo dala Moskva, vjeruje da bi imunitet bio poštovan.

Ipak nije sigurna da Zelenski u Moskvi „ima što tražiti“, jer bi mu Putin, šali se, „sat i pol pričao o povijesti“ i držao lekcije koje on više ne može slušati. Smatra da u takvim razgovorima uvijek mora postojati **posrednik**. Voditeljica dodaje da „ne smiju ih ostaviti same“, s čime se gošća slaže.

Ključna je, prema Polović, činjenica da ukrajinski predsjednik **gubi podršku na svim frontama**:

- nema više podršku kod kuće,
- nema je ni u vlastitoj političkoj stranci,
- gubi podršku Amerike,
- ni Europi više nije lako.

Kao primjer navodi posljednji summit Europskog vijeća. Zelenski je ponovno tražio novac i dodatna sredstva, što Polović ironično opisuje rečenicom „daj svemirski brod“. Tada je odbijen jer Europa naprosto više nije u mogućnosti. Nije čak ni jasno, dodaje, odakle se još vade svi ti novci za pomoć Ukrajini, a to situaciju u Europi čini **vrlo uzavrelom**.
sections.subtitle_en: Zelenskyy in Moscow? A President Losing Support on All Sides
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović speaks about the Ukrainian president's loss of support at home, in America, and in Europe
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether a trip by **Zelenskyy** to Moscow is possible, noting that some claim he is no longer even president due to the lack of elections. She also asks whether this would be good PR, with an invitation in the style of "come, you will be safe." Polović says with a laugh that these would be her "questions that ask a lot." Personally, she says, she wouldn't go.

She explains this by "very strange things" happening in the West, where America "abducts a president." The host observes that the West "has become wild." Polović adds that diplomatic immunity in the West, as shown, is not guaranteed to those declared dictators. If the guarantee were given by Moscow, she believes immunity would be respected.

Still, she is not sure that Zelenskyy "has any business being" in Moscow, because Putin, she jokes, "would talk to him about history for an hour and a half" and lecture him with lessons he can no longer bear to listen to. She believes that in such talks there must always be a **mediator**. The host adds that "they must not leave them alone," with which the guest agrees.

The key fact, according to Polović, is that the Ukrainian president is **losing support on all fronts**:

- he no longer has support at home,
- he doesn't have it in his own political party either,
- he is losing the support of America,
- nor is it easy for Europe anymore.

As an example, she cites the last European Council summit. Zelenskyy again asked for money and additional funds, which Polović ironically describes with the sentence "give me a spaceship." At that time he was turned down because Europe simply is no longer capable. It isn't even clear, she adds, where all this money to help Ukraine is still being pulled from, and that makes the situation in Europe **very volatile**.

> "Magisterium alignment:"

Note: The text does not conflict with Catholic moral teaching.

sections.subtitle: Lagarde odlazi, Macron u ECB, Orban u UN? Čakule s vrha svjetske politike
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća prenosi glasine da bi Macron nakon predsjedničkog mandata mogao preuzeti Europsku središnju banku
sections.content:
Voditeljica u šali pita je li **Christine Lagarde** zbog novca dala ostavku. Polović pojašnjava da je Lagarde zapravo najavila da će ostavku podnijeti u veljači sljedeće godine. Takve rokade naziva „malim igricama“. Lagarde se „šeta“ kroz međunarodne financijske institucije, a neke su osobe, kaže, jednostavno **„pretplaćene“ na takve pozicije**.

U tu skupinu ubraja i francuskog predsjednika **Macrona**. Smatra da se tijekom aktualnih nemira ponaša kao da ga se oni ne tiču, kao da nije predsjednik i nije odgovoran za ono što se događa u Francuskoj. „Kad već glumimo Nostradamusa“, prenosi i ono što, kako kaže, prepričavaju inozemni podcasteri, uz ogradu da su to „pomalo čakule“. Prema tim glasinama, Macron bi nakon predsjedničkog mandata trebao postati **predsjednik Europske središnje banke**. Bio bi to lijep nastavak karijere u svijetu iz kojeg je i došao, sada obogaćen predsjedničkim iskustvom.

Voditeljica zatim spominje priču koja je bila istaknuta u medijima: da bi **Orban** mogao postati šef Ujedinjenih naroda. Polović kaže da tu ideju gura Trump, iako „iznad duše mrzi“ Ujedinjene narode. Podsjeća da je Trump povukao bitan dio financiranja, a i uplate koje ostaju kasne. SAD su najveći uplatitelj i UN ovisi o njihovu novcu.

Trump se, kako kaže Polović, odjednom sjetio da bi Orbana mogao smjestiti na funkciju **glavnog tajnika**. Ta funkcija za njega možda i ne bi bila loša: Orban bi donio velike promjene i s te pozicije mogao **oblikovati svijet prema Trumpovoj viziji**. Voditeljica zaključuje da „svatko misli na svoga“, s čime se gošća slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Lagarde Leaves, Macron to the ECB, Orban to the UN? Gossip From the Top of World Politics
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest reports rumors that Macron could take over the European Central Bank after his presidential term
sections.content_en:
The host asks jokingly whether **Christine Lagarde** resigned because of money. Polović clarifies that Lagarde actually announced that she will submit her resignation in February of next year. She calls such reshuffles "little games." Lagarde "strolls" through international financial institutions, and some individuals, she says, are simply **"subscribed" to such positions**.

In that group she also includes French President **Macron**. She believes that during the current unrest he behaves as if it doesn't concern him, as if he isn't the president and isn't responsible for what is happening in France. "Since we are already playing Nostradamus," she also reports what, as she says, foreign podcasters are recounting, with the qualification that these are "somewhat gossip." According to these rumors, after his presidential term Macron is supposed to become **President of the European Central Bank**. It would be a nice career continuation in the world from which he came, now enriched with presidential experience.

The host then mentions a story that was highlighted in the media: that **Orban** could become head of the United Nations. Polović says that Trump is pushing that idea, even though he hates the United Nations "with all his heart." She recalls that Trump withdrew a significant portion of funding, and even the payments that remain are late. The US is the largest contributor and the UN depends on their money.

Trump, as Polović says, suddenly remembered that he could place Orban in the position of **Secretary-General**. That function might not be bad for him: Orban would bring major changes and from that position could **shape the world according to Trump's vision**. The host concludes that "everyone looks out for their own," with which the guest agrees.

sections.subtitle: Nasljednici Zelenskog i granice Trumpove moći
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović zaključuje da Trump nije bio dovoljno moćan da svrgne Zelenskog, ni da održi Orbana i Vučića
sections.content:
Prije nego što se vrati temi Francuske, voditeljica pita je li Zelenskom već pronađen nasljednik. Polović potvrđuje da se stalno vrti nekoliko imena. Među njima je **Zalužnij**, sada veleposlanik Ukrajine u Velikoj Britaniji, te **Budanov**.

Gošća podsjeća na turbulentne odnose Trumpa i Zelenskog. Nakon velike svađe u **Ovalnom uredu** odnosi su se neko vrijeme smirili. Nedavno ga je Trump, prema njezinim riječima, ponovno izvrijeđao i poručio mu da je vrijeme da ode s mjesta predsjednika. Kada se Zelenski oglušio o taj „savjet“, Trump je dodao da bi Ukrajina trebala predložiti neku drugu osobu za pregovore. Polović kaže da sve to postaje „neugodno“.

Iz toga izvodi zaključak koji smatra zanimljivim: **Trump očito nije dovoljno moćan da svrgne Zelenskog**. Vidi i širi obrazac:

- Trump nije uspio **svrgnuti Zelenskog**,
- nije bio dovoljno moćan da **održi Orbana**,
- čini se da nije uspio **održati ni Vučića**.

Iza toga Polović vidi dublji proces, **sraz globalizma i suverenizma u Europe**. Prema njezinoj ocjeni, ta borba određuje sudbinu političkih lidera na kontinentu, a pokazuje i da američki predsjednik ne može uvijek nametnuti rješenja kakva želi.
sections.subtitle_en: Zelenskyy's Successors and the Limits of Trump's Power
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović concludes that Trump was not powerful enough to overthrow Zelenskyy, nor to maintain Orban and Vučić
sections.content_en:
Before returning to the topic of France, the host asks whether a successor to Zelenskyy has already been found. Polović confirms that several names are constantly being circulated. Among them are **Zaluzhnyi**, now Ukraine's ambassador to the United Kingdom, and **Budanov**.

The guest recalls the turbulent relations between Trump and Zelenskyy. After a major argument in the **Oval Office**, relations calmed down for a while. Recently, Trump, according to her words, insulted him again and told him it was time to step down from the presidency. When Zelenskyy turned a deaf ear to that "advice," Trump added that Ukraine should propose another person for negotiations. Polović says all of this is becoming "uncomfortable."

From this she draws a conclusion she considers interesting: **Trump is obviously not powerful enough to overthrow Zelenskyy**. She sees a broader pattern as well:

- Trump did not manage to **overthrow Zelenskyy**,
- he was not powerful enough to **sustain Orban**,
- it seems he did not manage to **sustain Vučić either**.

Behind this Polović sees a deeper process, **the clash of globalism and sovereignism in Europe**. In her assessment, this struggle determines the fate of political leaders on the continent, and also shows that the American president cannot always impose the solutions he wants.
