sections.subtitle: „Donrova doktrina“ zapela u Brazilu: Trump ne može oblikovati svaki kontinent
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović objašnjava kako Trump mijenja vlade u Latinskoj Americi i gdje je ta politika zapela
sections.content:
Na kraju razgovora o Ukrajini i Zelenskom Jadranka Polović zaključuje da Trump nije bio dovoljno moćan da održi ni Orbana ni Vučića. U tome vidi širi **sraz globalizma i suverenizma**, a da bi to pokazala, vraća se izborima u Latinskoj Americi. Ta je regija posljednjih godinu dana poligon na kojem američki predsjednik primjenjuje ono što naziva **„Donrovom doktrinom“**.

Polović objašnjava da Trump ondje doslovno mijenja vlade i da mu je to isprva dobro krenulo. Prvo je bila Venezuela, a zatim su uslijedile promjene vlasti u nizu zemalja. Kao primjere navodi Čile, Ekvador (uz ogradu da joj se tako čini), Kolumbiju i Argentinu. Riječ je uglavnom o desničarskim vladama koje su vrlo sklone njegovoj politici i s kojima je u odličnim odnosima. Sve se to, naglašava, odvija **„pod krinkom borbe protiv narkokartela“**.

Trump je ipak zapeo na jednoj iznimno velikoj zemlji, Brazilu. U prvom krugu predsjedničkih izbora vodio je **Flavio Bolsonaro**, sin bivšeg predsjednika koji služi zatvorsku kaznu od 27 godina. U drugom se krugu situacija iznenađujuće preokrenula i pobjedu je odnio 81-godišnji De Silva.

Za Polović je to znak da je Donrova doktrina naišla na granicu i da Trump ne može oblikovati svijet posvuda. Opisuje ga kao političara koji je marketinški izvrsno potkovan, koji svoju viziju svijeta širi na sve strane i javnost uvjerava da je sve pod kontrolom. Unatoč tome, smatra ona, i dalje postoji **duboka država**, bilo globalna bilo američka, s globalističkim tendencijama. Ta struktura također utječe na zbivanja i Trumpu postavlja granice.
sections.subtitle_en: "Donroe Doctrine" Stuck in Brazil: Trump Cannot Shape Every Continent
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović explains how Trump changes governments in Latin America and where that policy got stuck
sections.content_en:
At the end of the conversation about Ukraine and Zelenskyy, Jadranka Polović concludes that Trump was not powerful enough to sustain either Orban or Vučić. In this she sees a broader **clash of globalism and sovereignism**, and to demonstrate this, she returns to the elections in Latin America. Over the past year, that region has been a testing ground where the American president applies what she calls the **"Donroe Doctrine"**.

Polović explains that Trump literally changes governments there and that things went well for him at first. First was Venezuela, and then changes of power followed in a series of countries. As examples, she cites Chile, Ecuador (with the caveat that it seems so to her), Colombia, and Argentina. These are mostly right-wing governments that are very receptive to his policy and with which he is on excellent terms. All of this, she emphasizes, takes place **"under the guise of the fight against drug cartels"**.

Trump nevertheless got stuck on one exceptionally large country, Brazil. In the first round of presidential elections, **Flávio Bolsonaro** led, the son of the former president who is serving a 27-year prison sentence. In the second round, the situation surprisingly reversed, and the victory was taken by 81-year-old De Silva.

For Polović, this is a sign that the Donroe Doctrine has encountered a limit and that Trump cannot shape the world everywhere. She describes him as a politician who is market-savvy, who spreads his vision of the world in all directions and convinces the public that everything is under control. Despite that, she believes, there still exists a **deep state**, whether global or American, with globalist tendencies. That structure also influences events and sets limits for Trump.

sections.subtitle: Trump protiv „njih“: Davos u sjeni, USAID ukinut, europski lideri na nišanu
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o padu važnosti Davosa i Trumpovoj želji da promijeni europske lidere
sections.content:
Voditeljica tu tezu odmah želi „pročačkati“. Pita je li točno shvatila da se na jednoj strani nalazi Trump, a na drugoj duboka država, globalna ili američka, svejedno. Pita i je li riječ o sukobu koji se vodi u svakom kutku svijeta. Jadranka Polović to potvrđuje, a nakon Latinske Amerike prelazi na Europu.

Europski su se lideri, podsjeća, godinama dogovarali u **Davosu** na skupu koji se održava početkom svake godine. Bio je to forum najmoćnijih ljudi na svijetu na kojem se kreirala svjetska politika. Otkako je Trump došao na vlast, Davos je pao u drugi plan i danas je „negdje u sjeni“.

Polović podsjeća i da je Trump **ukinuo USAID** i „potjerao Sorosa“, kojeg zato trenutačno nema u javnosti. Koliko zna, protiv njega su u SAD-u pokrenuti i neki sudski postupci.

Nije tajna, nastavlja ona, da je Trump vrlo zainteresiran za **promjenu europskih lidera**, koji mu doslovno idu na živce. Zato podržava stranke i političare koji su mu bliski:

- **Alternativu za Njemačku**,
- **Marine Le Pen**,
- do nedavno i **Meloni**, s kojom se nedavno „mrvicu“ posvađao, no Polović vjeruje da će se pomiriti,
- **Orbana**, kojeg je također podržavao.

Macrona, kaže gošća, Trump „nikako nije mogao“. Iako s njim načelno djeluje u dobrim odnosima, i njega bi rado zamijenio. Zaključak Polović glasi da je globalistička ideologija u Europi i dalje snažno prisutna. Zato nije sigurno da Trump može postavljati vlade po Europi kako mu padne na pamet.
sections.subtitle_en: Trump Against "Them": Davos in the Shadow, USAID Abolished, European Leaders in the Crosshairs
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the decline in the importance of Davos and Trump's desire to change European leaders
sections.content_en:
The host immediately wants to "dig into" that thesis. She asks whether she understood correctly that Trump is on one side, and on the other is the deep state, global or American, regardless. She also asks whether it is a conflict being waged in every corner of the world. Jadranka Polović confirms this, and after Latin America moves on to Europe.

European leaders, she recalls, for years conferred in **Davos** at the gathering held at the beginning of each year. It was a forum of the most powerful people in the world where global politics was shaped. Since Trump came to power, Davos has fallen into the background and is today "somewhere in the shadow."

Polović also recalls that Trump **abolished USAID** and "chased away Soros," which is why he is currently absent from the public eye. As far as she knows, certain court proceedings have also been initiated against him in the US.

It is no secret, she continues, that Trump is very interested in **changing European leaders**, who literally get on his nerves. That is why he supports parties and politicians close to him:

- **Alternative for Germany**,
- **Marine Le Pen**,
- until recently **Meloni** as well, with whom he recently had a "tiny" argument, but Polović believes they will reconcile,
- **Orban**, whom he also supported.

Macron, says the guest, Trump "could not stand at all." Even though on principle he seems to be on good terms with him, he would gladly replace him too. Polović's conclusion is that globalist ideology is still strongly present in Europe. Therefore, it is not certain that Trump can install governments across Europe however he pleases.

sections.subtitle: Orbanov odlazak kao pobjeda Bruxellesa
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović komentira odlazak Viktora Orbana i dolazak novog mađarskog lidera
sections.content:
Kao najjasniji dokaz da Trump ne može krojiti europske vlade Jadranka Polović navodi **Mađarsku**. Orbanov odlazak iz Budimpešte ocjenjuje kao veliku pobjedu **Europske komisije i Europskog vijeća**. Euroskepticizam i otpor politikama Europske unije koje je Orban širio dovodili su, objašnjava, u pitanje sam autoritet Unije.

Novi mađarski lider je **Peter Mađar**. Polović ističe da je on u velikoj mjeri odstupio od Orbanovih politika, ali da se o tome u javnosti malo čuje. Europska unija, dodaje, i dalje nastoji s njim „paktirati“.
sections.subtitle_en: Orban's Departure as a Victory for Brussels
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović comments on Viktor Orban's departure and the arrival of the new Hungarian leader
sections.content_en:
As the clearest proof that Trump cannot tailor European governments, Jadranka Polović cites **Hungary**. She assesses Orban's departure from Budapest as a great victory for the **European Commission and the European Council**. Euroscepticism and resistance to European Union policies spread by Orban called into question, she explains, the very authority of the Union.

The new Hungarian leader is **Péter Magyar**. Polović points out that he has deviated from Orban's policies to a large extent, but that little is heard about it in the public. The European Union, she adds, still seeks to "make a pact" with him.

sections.subtitle: Srbija između Washingtona i Bruxellesa: strateški dijalog, Đerdap 3 i čestitka Studentskoj listi
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava strateški sporazum SAD-a i Srbije te čestitku Bijele kuće Studentskoj listi
sections.content:
Posebno zanimljivim slučajem Jadranka Polović smatra **Srbiju**. Podsjeća da je Trump, svega mjesec ili nešto više prije izbora, sa Srbijom otvorio **strateški dijalog**. Strateški sporazum potpisan je, prema njezinu sjećanju, u srpnju. Obuhvaća visoke tehnologije, obrazovanje, energetiku i niz drugih područja.

Prema njezinoj ocjeni, bilo je posve vidljivo da **Sjedinjene Američke Države postupno preuzimaju kompletnu energetiku** na prostoru Srbije. U planu su bili gradnja nove hidroelektrane **Đerdap 3**, brojnih podatkovnih centara i projekti svemirskih istraživanja, dakle „veliki, veliki poslovi“.

Gošći je bila iznimno zanimljiva čestitka koju je **Bijela kuća** uputila **Studentskoj listi** nakon pobjede na izborima. U njoj se Washington toplo nada nastavku strateškog dijaloga, odnosno realizaciji svih dogovorenih projekata započetih pod Vučićevom administracijom.

Voditeljica primjećuje da Trumpu onda ne bi trebalo biti drago što je Vučić otišao. Polović se slaže, ali dodaje da je narod tako odlučio. Naglašava i da je u izbore „itekako bila uvučena“ Europska unija, koja je velika podrška Studentskoj listi.

Izbori su se, objašnjava ona, održali u kontekstu iznimno velikih turbulencija koje Srbiju tresu dvije godine, a zapravo i dulje. Podsjeća na velike prosvjede protiv **Rio Tinta** i kopanja litija, pri čemu je, prema njezinim riječima, upravo Europskoj uniji trebao taj rudnik. Spominje i prosvjede nakon ubojstva u osnovnoj školi **Ribnikar**. Sve je to, kaže, provociralo ljude i proizvelo **maksimalno destabilizirano društvo**. Ostaje veliko pitanje kako će se to odraziti na stabilnost zemlje.

Njezin je zaključak da se nad Srbijom, kao jednom od ključnih država regije, vodi borba za kontrolu između europskih država i američke administracije. Ti se interesi, smatra, ondje izravno sudaraju, iako se sve ne odvija javno.
sections.subtitle_en: Serbia Between Washington and Brussels: Strategic Dialogue, Đerdap 3, and Congratulations to the Students' List
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the US-Serbia strategic agreement and the White House's congratulations to the Students' List
sections.content_en:
Jadranka Polović considers **Serbia** a particularly interesting case. She recalls that Trump, merely a month or slightly more before the elections, opened a **strategic dialogue** with Serbia. The strategic agreement was signed, according to her memory, in July. It covers high technologies, education, energy, and a series of other areas.

In her assessment, it was entirely visible that the **United States of America is gradually taking over all energy infrastructure** across Serbia. Planned were the construction of the new hydroelectric power plant **Đerdap 3**, numerous data centers, and space research projects, hence "big, big business."

The guest found exceptionally interesting the congratulations that the **White House** sent to the **Students' List** after their election victory. In it, Washington warmly hopes for the continuation of the strategic dialogue, that is, the realization of all agreed projects initiated under Vučić's administration.

The host observes that Trump then shouldn't be pleased that Vučić has left. Polović agrees, but adds that the people decided that way. She also emphasizes that the European Union was "heavily involved" in the elections, providing great support to the Students' List.

The elections, she explains, took place in the context of exceptionally great turbulences that have been shaking Serbia for two years, and actually even longer. She recalls the large protests against **Rio Tinto** and lithium mining, whereby, according to her words, it was precisely the European Union that needed that mine. She also mentions the protests after the killings at the **Ribnikar** primary school. All of that, she says, provoked people and produced a **maximally destabilized society**. The big question remains how this will reflect on the stability of the country.

Her conclusion is that over Serbia, as one of the key states in the region, a struggle for control is being waged between European states and the American administration. Those interests, she believes, clash directly there, even though everything does not unfold publicly.

sections.subtitle: Ruski plin, europski uvjeti i „turski model“ Branka Milanovića
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović prenosi prijedlog ekonomista Branka Milanovića da Srbija slijedi primjer Turske
sections.content:
Na pitanje o ulozi Rusije Jadranka Polović odgovara da je i Moskva poslala **vrlo oštru poruku**. Srbija ovisi o **ruskom plinu**, pa je bilo veliko pitanje kako će se prema tome postaviti Studentska lista. Prema saznanjima gošće, to je jedan od prvih vanjskopolitičkih odgovora nove vlasti: zasad neće biti uvođenja sankcija Rusiji. Voditeljica dodaje da je to izjavio jedan od predstavnika liste. Polović upozorava da to nije sigurno, jer će Europa sigurno postaviti velike zahtjeve.

Gošća smatra da bi Europska unija trebala **geopolitički obuhvatiti Srbiju**. To ponekad znači i omekšati zahtjeve, primjerice oko **poglavlja 3** i njegova otvaranja te oko odnosa s **Kosovom**. Takva bi se pitanja, prema njezinu mišljenju, trebala rješavati postupno, kroz godine, kako bi se sačuvao entuzijazam za ulazak u Uniju, ako on još postoji.

Situaciju u Srbiji naziva vrlo zanimljivom i iznosi podatke:

- **više od 85 posto građana** ne podupire ulazak Srbije u NATO,
- iznimno raste broj onih koji su protiv Europske unije.

Pred izbore je, kaže, slušala **Branka Milanovića**, svjetski poznatog i vrlo utjecajnog američko-srpskog ekonomista. On smatra da bi Srbija trebala napraviti isto što radi **Turska**. Srbija oko dvije trećine vanjskotrgovinske razmjene ostvaruje s Europskom unijom. Milanović ipak drži da nikada neće moći do kraja ispuniti zahtjeve Unije. Uvijek će se, prema njegovoj procjeni, naći **10 do 12 država članica**, među njima i **Hrvatska**, koje će odbiti ratificirati sporazum o pristupanju.

Zato Milanović predlaže da se sporazumom formalizira **odustajanje od članstva**, uz nastavak široke suradnje u svakom pogledu. Voditeljica zaključuje da je to baš kao slučaj Turske, što gošća potvrđuje.
sections.subtitle_en: Russian Gas, European Conditions, and Branko Milanović's "Turkish Model"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović conveys the proposal of economist Branko Milanović that Serbia follow the example of Turkey
sections.content_en:
To the question about the role of Russia, Jadranka Polović replies that Moscow also sent a **very sharp message**. Serbia depends on **Russian gas**, so it was a big question how the Students' List would position itself toward that. According to the guest's findings, that is one of the first foreign policy responses of the new government: for now there will be no introduction of sanctions on Russia. The host adds that this was stated by one of the representatives of the list. Polović warns that this is not certain, because Europe will surely pose great demands.

The guest believes that the European Union should **geopolitically encompass Serbia**. This sometimes also means softening demands, for example regarding **Chapter 3** and its opening, and regarding relations with **Kosovo**. Such issues, according to her opinion, should be resolved gradually, over the years, in order to preserve enthusiasm for joining the Union, if it still exists.

She calls the situation in Serbia very interesting and presents the data:

- **more than 85 percent of citizens** do not support Serbia's accession to NATO,
- the number of those who are against the European Union is growing exceptionally.

Before the elections, she says, she listened to **Branko Milanović**, the world-renowned and very influential American-Serbian economist. He believes that Serbia should do the same thing that **Turkey** is doing. Serbia conducts about two-thirds of its foreign trade with the European Union. Milanović nevertheless maintains that it will never be able to fully satisfy the Union's demands. In his estimate, there will always be **10 to 12 member states**, among them **Hrvatska**, that will refuse to ratify the accession treaty.

Therefore, Milanović proposes that a treaty formalize **giving up on membership**, while continuing broad cooperation in every respect. The host concludes that it is just like the case of Turkey, which the guest confirms.

sections.subtitle: Podjela svijeta na sfere: Trumpu „nikad dosta“
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o američkoj strategiji nacionalne sigurnosti i zapadnoj hemisferi
sections.content:
Voditeljica u šali pita jesu li Putin i Trump „već napravili križaljku“ i za ovaj dio Europe. Zamišlja kako Melanija suprugu govori da Slovenija ostane „njihova“, a za ostalo da je baš briga. Ozbiljno pak pita jesu li u ovom dijelu kontinenta već povučene linije sfera utjecaja.

Jadranka Polović odgovara da se **na Trumpa ne može računati**. Podsjeća na američku **strategiju nacionalne sigurnosti** usvojenu, prema njezinu sjećanju, 25. studenoga, u kojoj je naglasak stavljen na **zapadnu hemisferu**. Što sve u nju ulazi, ostalo je otvoreno. Europa svakako ulazi, ali su se pojavili i problemi poput **Grenlanda**, sada i **Islanda**, te **Kanade**.

Polović smatra da bi Kina i Rusija vrlo rado podijelile interesne sfere. Trumpu je, međutim, **„nikad dosta“**. Ono što je zapisano samo je početna pozicija, a ako može ući u tuđe dvorište, učinit će to vrlo rado, i to već radi.

Trump je trenutačno zauzet **Bliskim istokom**, koji želi preurediti. Taj preustroj, podsjeća gošća, traje još od zaljevskog rata 1991. Cilj mu je stvoriti sigurno okruženje za **Izrael**, pravog saveznika SAD-a u regiji. Pritom ističe iznimno snažan utjecaj židovskog lobija i u samim Sjedinjenim Državama. Kad i ako sredi Bliski istok, posebno Iran, Trump će prema njezinoj procjeni krenuti prema **Aziji**. Riječ je o **Tajvanu**, ali i o široj regiji koju Kina smatra svojim interesnim područjem.

Na njegovu se riječ, ponavlja Polović, ne može osloniti, jer ono što danas kaže sutra porekne, preoblikuje ili proširi. Voditeljica zaključuje da će, kako god bilo, biti napeto, s čime se gošća slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Division of the World into Spheres: Trump "Can Never Get Enough"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the US national security strategy and the Western Hemisphere
sections.content_en:
The host jokingly asks whether Putin and Trump have "already done the crossword puzzle" for this part of Europe as well. She imagines Melania telling her husband to let Slovenia remain "theirs," and not to care about the rest. Seriously, though, she asks whether lines of spheres of influence have already been drawn in this part of the continent.

Jadranka Polović replies that **Trump cannot be counted on**. She recalls the American **national security strategy** adopted, according to her memory, on November 25, in which emphasis was placed on the **Western Hemisphere**. What all falls into it remained open. Europe certainly falls into it, but problems have also emerged such as **Greenland**, now **Iceland** as well, and **Canada**.

Polović believes that China and Russia would very gladly divide spheres of interest. Trump, however, **"can never get enough"**. What is written down is only a starting position, and if he can enter someone else's yard, he will do so very gladly, and is already doing so.

Trump is currently preoccupied with the **Middle East**, which he wants to reorganize. That restructuring, the guest recalls, has been going on since the Gulf War of 1991. Its goal is to create a secure environment for **Israel**, the true ally of the US in the region. In doing so, she emphasizes the exceptionally strong influence of the Jewish lobby in the United States itself. When and if he settles the Middle East, especially Iran, Trump will, according to her estimate, move toward **Asia**. This concerns **Taiwan**, but also the wider region that China considers its area of interest.

One cannot rely on his word, Polović repeats, because what he says today, tomorrow he denies, reshapes, or expands. The host concludes that, however it may be, it will be tense, with which the guest agrees.

sections.subtitle: Francuska u plamenu: periferne škole, ubijeni profesor i granice asimilacijskog modela
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović analizira uzroke prosvjeda u francuskim školama na periferiji
sections.content:
Voditeljica se vraća ranijoj opasci gošće da se **Macron** tijekom nemira ponaša kao da prosvjeda u Francuskoj nema. Podsjeća i na Trumpovu izjavu da **„islam želi uništiti Francusku“** te da je Emmanuelu poručio neka brine o svojoj zemlji jer je uskoro u takvom obliku više neće imati. Macron je to demantirao. Voditeljica zato pita što se zapravo dogodilo: jesu li posrijedi islamisti, posljedica neumjerenih migracija ili su se doista pobunili učenici i studenti.

Jadranka Polović ne želi ponavljati poznatu priču o francuskoj **kulturi pobune** koja seže do Francuske revolucije. Ističe da je sve počelo u **perifernim školama**, gimnazijama i srednjim školama na periferiji. Situacija u tim školama, kaže, zaista je loša. Kao nastavnik u takvoj školi „imate glavu u torbi“ i nikad ne znate što će se dogoditi. Upravo je tako ubijen profesor, kako se prisjeća, geografije i povijesti **Samuel Paty**. Nastavnika nedostaje, a mnogi od njih dolaze iz sjeverne Afrike, iz Alžira, Maroka i drugih zemalja, što je također problem.

Gošća ipak upozorava da se francuski problem **ne može svesti samo na migracije**, iako je riječ o nekontroliranim migracijama. Francuska je bila velika kolonijalna sila koja je držala sjever Afrike i Sahel. Odande dolazi velik broj migranata koji dobro govore francuski i relativno lako dobivaju državljanstvo. Francuska pritom primjenjuje **asimilacijski model**: svi došljaci trebaju se prije svega osjećati kao građani Francuske. Manjinska obilježja smiju zadržati, ali ne u javnom prostoru.

Val prosvjeda, kaže Polović, proširio se na **Belgiju**, **Italiju** i druge zemlje, a prosvjeduje se i u **Albaniji**. Voditeljica dodaje Španjolsku. Gošća spominje tešku nesreću koja se ondje dogodila dan ranije, već drugu po redu. Ona prema njezinim riječima ukazuje na loše stanje javne infrastrukture u jednoj velikoj i moćnoj državi.
sections.subtitle_en: France in Flames: Peripheral Schools, Murdered Teacher, and the Limits of the Assimilation Model
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović analyzes the causes of protests in French peripheral schools
sections.content_en:
The host returns to the guest's earlier remark that **Macron** behaves during the unrest as if there are no protests in France. She also recalls Trump's statement that **"Islam wants to destroy France"** and that he told Emmanuel to look after his country because soon he won't have it in such a form anymore. Macron denied this. The host therefore asks what actually happened: is it Islamists, a consequence of excessive migration, or did pupils and students truly rebel.

Jadranka Polović does not want to repeat the familiar story about the French **culture of rebellion** dating back to the French Revolution. She emphasizes that everything started in **peripheral schools**, gymnasiums and secondary schools on the outskirts. The situation in those schools, she says, is truly bad. As a teacher in such a school "you have your neck on the line" and you never know what will happen. That is precisely how a teacher, as she recalls, of geography and history, **Samuel Paty**, was murdered. There is a shortage of teachers, and many of them come from North Africa, from Algeria, Morocco, and other countries, which is also a problem.

The guest nevertheless warns that the French problem **cannot be reduced solely to migrations**, even though uncontrolled migrations are involved. France was a major colonial power that held North Africa and the Sahel. From there comes a large number of migrants who speak French well and obtain citizenship relatively easily. France at the same time applies an **assimilation model**: all newcomers should primarily feel like citizens of France. They are allowed to retain minority characteristics, but not in public space.

The wave of protests, Polović says, has spread to **Belgium**, **Italy**, and other countries, and protests are taking place in **Albania** as well. The host adds Spain. The guest mentions a serious accident that occurred there the previous day, already the second in a row. It, in her words, points to the poor condition of public infrastructure in a large and powerful country.

sections.subtitle: 10 posto ljudi drži 75 posto bogatstva: zajednički nazivnik europskih nemira
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća iznosi podatke iz World Inequality Reporta o globalnoj nejednakosti
sections.content:
Iza svih tih prosvjeda Jadranka Polović vidi **zajednički nazivnik**. Riječ je ponajprije o nemirima **socioekonomskog karaktera**, a problem je u ekonomskom sustavu koji traži radikalni zaokret.

Kao dokaz navodi **World Inequality Report za 2026.**, koji se odnosi na 2025. godinu. Prema tom izvješću **svega 10 posto svjetske populacije raspolaže sa 75 posto svjetskog bogatstva**. Godinama se, pa i u Hrvatskoj, govori o rastu BDP-a, objašnjava gošća. Globalizacija i tehnološki napredak doista donose rast produktivnosti i stvaraju enormno bogatstvo. Ono se, međutim, koncentrira u rukama iznimno malog broja ljudi. Globalna nejednakost i nejednakost unutar država tako postaju **političko pitanje**.

Polović smatra da je potreban **radikalni zaokret od neoliberalnih politika**, uz promjenu političkog i ekonomskog sustava. Iz svoje akademske pozicije upozorava da takva rasprava gotovo ne postoji i da se ne nude alternativni modeli. Kao primjer pogrešnog pristupa navodi Macronovu najavu da će u francusko školstvo uložiti 5 milijardi eura. Problem nije u tome, kaže, nego je sustav potrebno potpuno promijeniti.

Podsjeća da su prosvjedi mladih zahvatili cijeli svijet. Počeli su u **Mongoliji** početkom 2025., a nastavili se u **Nepalu**, na **Filipinima** i u **Paragvaju**, da bi stigli i u Europu. Mlada generacija postaje svjesna da ima **problem stanovanja** i da si mnogi ne mogu priuštiti stan, koji bi trebao biti temeljno ljudsko pravo. Jednako tako postaje svjesna problema s dostupnošću javnih usluga.

Kao rijedak primjer alternativnog promišljanja Polović izdvaja francuskog ekonomista i društvenog teoretičara **Thomasa Piketija**, autora djela ***Kapital u 21. stoljeću***, koje je prevedeno i u Hrvatskoj. Piketi zagovara **porez na bogatstvo i dobit na globalnoj razini**. Razlog objašnjava na primjeru: ako takav porez uvede samo Hrvatska, kapital će otići u Sloveniju ili neku drugu državu s drukčijim poreznim sustavom.

Iz njegova rada gošća izdvaja i tezu da **meritokracija više ne može osigurati napredak**. Tko se oslanja na vlastite sposobnosti, znanje i obrazovanje, koliko god u njih uložio, neće mnogo napredovati. Temelj bogatstva danas je **rentijerstvo**, odnosno ulaganje u imovinu, nekretnine i zemljišta, što se, kaže, vidi i u Hrvatskoj.

Njezin recept uključuje:

- radikalni zaokret od neoliberalizma i **politike štednje**,
- **pravednu raspodjelu dohotka**,
- ulaganje u **javne usluge** i njihovu dostupnost građanima,
- **nacionalizaciju imovine** najbogatijih, osobito kada je riječ o strateškim resursima.
sections.subtitle_en: 10 Percent of People Hold 75 Percent of Wealth: The Common Denominator of European Unrest
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest presents data from the World Inequality Report on global inequality
sections.content_en:
Behind all these protests, Jadranka Polović sees a **common denominator**. It is primarily a matter of unrest of a **socioeconomic character**, and the problem lies in an economic system that demands a radical shift.

As proof, she cites the **World Inequality Report for 2026**, which pertains to the year 2025. According to that report, **a mere 10 percent of the world's population holds 75 percent of the world's wealth**. For years, including in Croatia, people have talked about GDP growth, the guest explains. Globalization and technological progress indeed bring productivity growth and create enormous wealth. It is, however, concentrated in the hands of an exceptionally small number of people. Global inequality and inequality within states thus become a **political issue**.

Polović believes that a **radical turnaround from neoliberal policies** is needed, along with a change in the political and economic system. From her academic position, she warns that such a discussion practically does not exist and that alternative models are not being offered. As an example of an erroneous approach, she cites Macron's announcement that he will invest 5 billion euros in the French school system. The problem is not in that, she says, but rather the system needs to be completely changed.

She recalls that youth protests have engulfed the whole world. They began in **Mongolia** at the start of 2025, and continued in **Nepal**, the **Philippines**, and **Paraguay**, before arriving in Europe as well. The young generation is becoming aware that it has a **housing problem** and that many cannot afford an apartment, which should be a fundamental human right. Likewise, it is becoming aware of problems with the accessibility of public services.

As a rare example of alternative thinking, Polović highlights the French economist and social theorist **Thomas Piketty**, author of the work ***Capital in the Twenty-First Century***, which was translated in Croatia as well. Piketty advocates a **tax on wealth and profit at the global level**. She explains the reason with an example: if only Croatia introduces such a tax, capital will flee to Slovenia or another country with a different tax system.

From his work, the guest also singles out the thesis that **meritocracy can no longer guarantee progress**. Whoever relies on their own abilities, knowledge, and education, no matter how much they invest in them, will not advance much. The foundation of wealth today is **rentierism**, that is, investing in property, real estate, and land, which, she says, is also seen in Croatia.

Her recipe includes:

- a radical turnaround from neoliberalism and **austerity policies**,
- **equitable distribution of income**,
- investment in **public services** and their accessibility to citizens,
- **nationalization of assets** of the wealthiest, especially when it comes to strategic resources.

sections.subtitle: „Svi smo u ovome zajedno“, samo netko na jahti: revolucija koja se neće dogoditi
sections.screenshot_description: Voditeljica i gošća u duhovitoj razmjeni o „pozivu na revoluciju“ i Arapskom proljeću
sections.content:
Voditeljica pita tko bi takvu promjenu uopće mogao provesti. Podsjeća na pandemiju i slogan **„svi smo u ovome zajedno“**, dok je netko bio na svojoj jahti, a netko u stanu od 50 kvadrata. Jadranka Polović dodaje da su mnogi bili i na ulici.

Europske političke elite, kaže gošća, ne pridaju tome pozornost i uopće ne razmišljaju o promjeni samog poretka. Ono što predlaže zapravo podrazumijeva **revoluciju**, koja se, nažalost, neće dogoditi. Voditeljica primjećuje kako „nježna gospođa“ zapravo poziva na revoluciju.

Polović objašnjava zašto ne vjeruje u takav ishod: slične situacije već su viđene. Podsjeća na **Arapsko proljeće 2011.** i na brojna nadanja mladih u zemljama sjeverne Afrike, Bahreinu i Emiratima. Ljudi su vjerovali da mogu promijeniti sustav. Ne samo da ga nisu promijenili, nego je situacija danas, kako kaže, „debelo gora“.
sections.subtitle_en: "We Are All in This Together", Only Someone on a Yacht: A Revolution That Will Not Happen
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host and guest in a humorous exchange about a "call to revolution" and the Arab Spring
sections.content_en:
The host asks who could carry out such a change at all. She recalls the pandemic and the slogan **"we are all in this together"**, while someone was on their yacht, and someone else in an apartment of 50 square meters. Jadranka Polović adds that many were on the street as well.

European political elites, the guest says, pay no attention to this and do not think at all about changing the order itself. What she proposes actually implies a **revolution**, which, unfortunately, will not happen. The host observes how a "gentle lady" is actually calling for revolution.

Polović explains why she does not believe in such an outcome: similar situations have already been seen. She recalls the **Arab Spring of 2011** and the numerous hopes of young people in the countries of North Africa, Bahrain, and the Emirates. People believed they could change the system. Not only did they not change it, but the situation today, as she says, is "vastly worse."

sections.subtitle: Mladi ne žele rat: otpor remilitarizaciji i regrutaciji
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović govori o uvođenju vojnog roka i prosvjedima protiv regrutacije u Njemačkoj
sections.content:
Kao drugi ključni razlog nemira po Europi Jadranka Polović navodi **otpor remilitarizaciji** i ratovima u Ukrajini, Gazi i Iranu. Na prosvjedima je, kaže, mnogo **propalestinskih zastava**, a ljudi time pokazuju otpor „besmislenim ratovima“. Voditeljica upozorava da ih pojedini komentatori odmah povezuju s Hamasom, ljevičarima i antifom. Polović odbacuje takvo pojednostavljenje.

Njezina je teza da se **moralni teret rata svaljuje na leđa mlade generacije**. Mnoge europske zemlje ponovno uvode **vojni rok** i pripremaju stanovništvo za rat. Kao primjer spominje članak o velikim ulaganjima **Nizozemske** u naoružanje, kojima se ta zemlja priprema za „veliki rat“. Politički lideri bi, smatra gošća, građanima trebali jasno objasniti o kakvom je ratu riječ i tko je neprijatelj. Kad se kao odgovor spomene **Rusija**, Polović pita može li se takav rat izbjeći i riješiti diplomatski.

Navodi i da se, kako je vidjela, 31. pripremaju **velike demonstracije u Njemačkoj protiv regrutacije**, a poziv na njih kruži internetom. Mlade generacije, objašnjava, nisu pripremljene za rat i ne žele ga. Odrasle su u opuštenom okruženju, u životu koji je izgledao posve drukčije. Pita kako bi izgledao život u ratu, u hladnim stanovima i bez energije. Voditeljica dodaje da se tada ne bi moglo spavati do podneva, a možda ne bi bilo ni društvenih mreža.

Gošća spominje i intervjue **Julije Mendel**, za koju misli da je bila glasnogovornica ureda Zelenskog. Mendel opisuje kako cijela generacija ukrajinske djece odrasta potpuno asocijalno, zatvorena u kućama, bez kontakata i bez normalnog odlaska u školu zbog neprestanih napada. Rusi, kaže Polović, ovih dana nevjerojatno gađaju Kijev i druge gradove, pa takvo ratno stanje naprosto treba završiti. Voditeljica zaključuje da će generacije biti uništene, i to ne samo gubitkom života nego i gubitkom zdravog razuma.
sections.subtitle_en: Young People Do Not Want War: Resistance to Remilitarization and Recruitment
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović speaks about the introduction of compulsory military service and protests against recruitment in Germany
sections.content_en:
As a second key reason for unrest across Europe, Jadranka Polović cites **resistance to remilitarization** and to the wars in Ukraine, Gaza, and Iran. At the protests, she says, there are many **pro-Palestinian flags**, and by this people are showing resistance to "pointless wars." The host warns that certain commentators immediately link them to Hamas, leftists, and antifa. Polović rejects such an oversimplification.

Her thesis is that the **moral burden of war is being placed on the shoulders of the young generation**. Many European countries are reintroducing **compulsory military service** and preparing the population for war. As an example, she mentions an article about large investments by the **Netherlands** in armaments, with which that country is preparing for a "great war." Political leaders should, the guest believes, clearly explain to citizens what kind of war this is and who the enemy is. When **Russia** is mentioned as the answer, Polović asks whether such a war can be avoided and resolved diplomatically.

She also states that, as she has seen, on the 31st **large demonstrations against recruitment in Germany** are being prepared, and an invitation to them is circulating on the internet. Young generations, she explains, are not prepared for war and do not want it. They grew up in a relaxed environment, in a life that looked completely different. She asks what life in war would look like, in cold apartments and without energy. The host adds that then one would not be able to sleep until noon, and perhaps there would be no social networks either.

The guest also mentions interviews with **Yuliia Mendel**, who she thinks was a spokesperson for Zelensky's office. Mendel describes how an entire generation of Ukrainian children is growing up completely asocial, shut up in houses, without contacts and without normally attending school due to constant attacks. The Russians, Polović says, are these days hitting Kyiv and other cities incredibly, so such a state of war simply must end. The host concludes that generations will be destroyed, and not only through the loss of life but also through the loss of sound mind.

sections.subtitle: „Snažni ljudi stvaraju dobra vremena“: Europa detanta i njezini veliki lideri
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća se prisjeća europskih lidera iz doba detanta
sections.content:
Voditeljica podsjeća na često citiranu misao, uz ogradu da se vjerojatno pripisuje pogrešnoj osobi: **snažni ljudi stvaraju dobra vremena, dobra vremena stvaraju slabe ljude, a slabi ljudi stvaraju loša vremena**, čime se krug zatvara.

Jadranka Polović smatra da je to možda najbolji opis europske povijesti od Drugog svjetskog rata. Nakon rata Europa je imala nekoliko jakih lidera koji su pridonijeli **detantu**. Nakon **Kubanske raketne krize**, kada se svijet našao na rubu propasti, za smirivanje nisu bili zaslužni samo **Hruščov i Kennedy**. Zaslužna je bila cijela generacija lidera, od **Willyja Brandta** do **generala De Gaullea**.

Europa je tada, kaže gošća, krenula putem koji ju je ostavio pod velikim utjecajem Sjedinjenih Američkih Država. Ipak je uspjela izgraditi **neobično snažan identitet**, prepoznat u svjetskim razmjerima. Bila je ekonomska sila, ali i ozbiljan **geopolitički akter**.
sections.subtitle_en: "Strong Men Create Good Times": The Europe of Détente and Its Great Leaders
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recalls European leaders from the era of détente
sections.content_en:
The host recalls an oft-quoted thought, with the caveat that it is probably attributed to the wrong person: **strong men create good times, good times create weak men, and weak men create bad times**, thereby closing the circle.

Jadranka Polović believes that this is perhaps the best description of European history since the Second World War. After the war, Europe had several strong leaders who contributed to **détente**. After the **Cuban Missile Crisis**, when the world found itself on the brink of ruin, it was not only **Khrushchev and Kennedy** who were credited with calming things down. The credit belonged to an entire generation of leaders, from **Willy Brandt** to **General De Gaulle**.

Europe then, says the guest, embarked on a path that left it under the great influence of the United States of America. Yet it still managed to build an **unusually strong identity**, recognized on a global scale. It was an economic power, but also a serious **geopolitical actor**.

sections.subtitle: Gdje je puklo: od Iraka i „stare Europe“ do Merkeličina „Mi to možemo“
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović kritički govori o političkom naslijeđu Angele Merkel
sections.content:
Voditeljica otkriva da je slično pitanje postavila i **Zekerijahu Smajiću**, koji je govorio o istoj temi. Pita kada je Europa, nakon moćnih političara i vojskovođa poput De Gaullea, počela „rađati“ ovakve političare kao danas. Zanima je i postoji li presudni trenutak u kojem su stari asovi otišli, a novi nisu imali od koga učiti.

Jadranka Polović presudni trenutak smješta **početkom 21. stoljeća**, kada je krenula serija vojno-humanitarnih intervencija, osobito u **Iraku 2003.** Njemačka i Francuska tada su odbile sudjelovati, nakon čega ih je **George Bush mlađi** nazvao **„starom Europom“**. Slijedile su ga nove zemlje, današnje članice Europske unije, koje su za to nagrađene ulaskom u NATO već 2004.

Uslijedio je, kaže, cijeli niz lidera. Mnogi bi među njima izdvojili **Angelu Merkel**, ali Polović je „po ničemu“ ne bi izdvojila kao veliku političarku. Podsjeća na **aferu prisluškivanja**, kada su prisluškivani gotovo svi europski lideri, uključujući Merkel, koja nije reagirala iako je riječ bila o nečuvenom slučaju. Merkel je, prema njezinoj ocjeni, upravo osoba koja je Europsku uniju uvela u problem. Nekritički je otvorila granice izgovorivši čuvenu rečenicu **„Da, mi to možemo“** i pustila u Europu nekoliko milijuna ljudi bez dokumenata. Nakon toga uslijedio je niz terorističkih napada.

Prije toga Europu je pogodila velika **gospodarska kriza** koja se preselila iz SAD-a. Dok se Amerika oporavljala, europske zemlje upale su u krizu i nakon 2008. nikada se do kraja nisu oporavile. **Politika štednje** najprije je primijenjena na novim članicama iz istočne Europe, a potom je postala model ekonomije i političke vlasti u zapadnoj Europi.

Zatim su uslijedili pandemija i rat u Ukrajini. Cijela generacija lidera, zaključuje Polović, nijedan od tih problema nije riješila, nego ih je samo produbila. Sada je to „došlo na naplatu“ i vidi se da Europa ovako ne može dalje.
sections.subtitle_en: Where It Broke: From Iraq and "Old Europe" to Merkel's "We Can Do It"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović speaks critically about the political legacy of Angela Merkel
sections.content_en:
The host reveals that she posed a similar question to **Zekerijah Smajić**, who spoke on the same topic. She asks when Europe, after powerful politicians and military commanders like De Gaulle, began "giving birth" to politicians such as those today. She is also interested in whether there is a decisive moment when the old aces departed, and the new ones had no one to learn from.

Jadranka Polović places the decisive moment at the **beginning of the 21st century**, when a series of military-humanitarian interventions began, especially in **Iraq in 2003**. Germany and France then refused to participate, after which **George Bush Jr.** called them **"old Europe"**. They were followed by new countries, today's members of the European Union, which were rewarded for this by entering NATO as early as 2004.

There followed, she says, an entire series of leaders. Many among them would single out **Angela Merkel**, but Polović "by no means" would single her out as a great politician. She recalls the **wiretapping affair**, when almost all European leaders were wiretapped, including Merkel, who did not react even though it was an unheard-of case. Merkel is, according to her assessment, precisely the person who led the European Union into trouble. She uncritically opened the borders, uttering the famous sentence **"Yes, we can do it"** and let several million people into Europe without documents. After that, a series of terrorist attacks followed.

Before that, Europe was hit by a major **economic crisis** that moved over from the USA. While America was recovering, European countries fell into crisis and after 2008 never fully recovered. The **austerity policy** was first applied to the new member states from Eastern Europe, and then became the model of economy and political rule in Western Europe.

Then followed the pandemic and the war in Ukraine. An entire generation of leaders, Polović concludes, solved none of these problems, but only deepened them. Now this has "come due for payment" and it is evident that Europe cannot go on like this.

sections.subtitle: Strah za budućnost: Europa na putu prema građanskom ratu?
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o eseju Davida Batesa i dubokoj polarizaciji europskih društava
sections.content:
Jadranka Polović otvoreno priznaje da je **iskreno strah za budućnost**. Nedavno je objavila tekst o britanskom znanstveniku **Davidu Batesu**, autoru dvaju velikih eseja pod zajedničkim naslovom **„Europska unija ide prema građanskom ratu“**.

Smatra da europska društva dolaze u stanje u kojem su **iznimno polarizirana oko svega**. To se vidi i u svakodnevnim odnosima: zbog bilo kakve političke rasprave ili stava ljudi „skaču na noževe“. Trebat će, kaže, mnogo vremena da se Europa vrati stanju iz uvodne rečenice podcasta. Najsretnija su, naime, ona vremena u kojima ljudi ne znaju tko im je predsjednik.

Voditeljica zaključuje da to znači da su ljudi danas jako nesretni, što gošća potvrđuje. Zato se, objašnjava, građani snažno mobiliziraju oko izbora, svake izbore doživljavaju kao referendum, a izlaznost je znatno porasla. To pokazuje da ljudi iskreno žele promjenu, iako Polović nije sigurna da će do nje doći.
sections.subtitle_en: Fear for the Future: Europe on the Way Toward Civil War?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the essay by David Bates and the deep polarization of European societies
sections.content_en:
Jadranka Polović openly admits that she is **sincerely afraid for the future**. Recently she published a text about the British scholar **David Bates**, the author of two major essays under the shared title **"The European Union Is Heading Toward Civil War"**.

She considers that European societies are entering a state in which they are **extremely polarized over everything**. This can be seen in everyday relations as well: over any kind of political debate or stance people "jump at knives." It will take, she says, a lot of time for Europe to return to the state from the podcast's opening sentence. The happiest times, namely, are those in which people do not know who their president is.

The host concludes that this means people today are very unhappy, which the guest confirms. That is why, she explains, citizens strongly mobilize around elections, they perceive every election as a referendum, and turnout has significantly increased. This shows that people sincerely want change, although Polović is not sure that it will come to pass.

sections.subtitle: Hrvatska diplomacija talac „dvaju brda“
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović govori o sukobu predsjednika i premijera i neimenovanim veleposlanicima
sections.content:
Pri kraju razgovora voditeljica pita kako se Hrvatska i njezina diplomacija snalaze u ovim zbivanjima. Jadranka Polović odgovara da postoji **ozbiljan problem u odnosu „dvaju brda“**, predsjednika i premijera. Zbog toga godinama nisu imenovani **veleposlanici**, čak ni u važnim državama, što smatra velikim hendikepom. Voditeljica ironično dodaje da je to možda nova politika: stavi pod tepih dok se oni ne potuku.

O **Ukrajini** predsjednik i premijer imaju dijametralno suprotna stajališta. Polović smatra da bi Hrvatska trebala zauzeti realne pozicije i procijeniti do koje mjere još može pomagati Ukrajini, a kada ta pomoć postaje beskorisna. Oba bi se dužnosnika, smatra, trebala **diplomatski angažirati u zaustavljanju rata**, koji je najveću štetu nanio Ukrajini, a zatim i Europi.

O nedavnim izborima u **Bosni i Hercegovini** kaže da je situacija i dalje zabrinjavajuća. Ipak je status hrvatskog naroda malo unaprijeđen, što ocjenjuje kao napredak. Sa **Srbijom** i **Crnom Gorom** Hrvatska bi, prema njezinu mišljenju, diplomacijom trebala rješavati brojna otvorena pitanja, i to **bez vanjskih tutora**.
sections.subtitle_en: Croatian Diplomacy Hostage to "Two Hills"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović speaks about the conflict between the president and the prime minister and unnamed ambassadors
sections.content_en:
Near the end of the conversation, the host asks how Croatia and its diplomacy are managing in these developments. Jadranka Polović replies that there is a **serious problem in the relationship between the "two hills"**, the president and the prime minister. Because of this, for years **ambassadors** have not been appointed, even to important countries, which she considers a great handicap. The host ironically adds that this is perhaps a new policy: sweep it under the carpet until they beat each other up.

On **Ukraine**, the president and the prime minister have diametrically opposed stances. Polović considers that Croatia should adopt realistic positions and assess to what extent it can still help Ukraine, and when that aid becomes useless. Both officials, she believes, should **engage diplomatically in stopping the war**, which has caused the greatest damage to Ukraine, and then to Europe as well.

Regarding the recent elections in **Bosnia and Herzegovina**, she says that the situation is still worrying. Nevertheless, the status of the Croatian people has been improved a little, which she evaluates as progress. With **Serbia** and **Montenegro**, Croatia should, in her opinion, resolve numerous open issues through diplomacy, and that **without external tutors**.
keywords_en: conflict between the president and the prime minister

sections.subtitle: Okršaj vanjskih tutora na Balkanu: novi akteri izbacuju stare
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća nabraja vanjske sile koje se bore za utjecaj u regiji
sections.content:
Vanjskih tutora u regiji, ističe Jadranka Polović, ima nevjerojatno mnogo, a neki od njih slabe. Nabraja ih:

- **SAD** i **Europska unija**, prisutni već 30 godina,
- **Rusija**, koja „nešto šalta po regiji“, ali sve manje,
- **Turska**, vrlo ozbiljan akter,
- **Izrael**, novi igrač koji itekako utječe na prilike,
- **Velika Britanija**, na koju se često zaboravi jer je uvijek tiha.

Novi akteri, kaže gošća, izbacuju stare. U regiji traje **okršaj** u kojem SAD, Velika Britanija, Turska i Izrael, iako međusobno nisu u dobrim odnosima, nastoje potisnuti utjecaj Europske unije, prvenstveno **Njemačke**. Francuska se drži, a Polović kao dokaz navodi da je **Macron** nedavno ugostio **Vučića**.

Bilo bi jako dobro, smatra gošća, kada bi Hrvatska **pogurala ulazak Crne Gore i Srbije u Europsku uniju**. Cijelo bi područje time bilo geopolitički zaokruženo i stabilizirano. Zalaže se za mnogo više dogovora i sastanaka lidera iz regije koji bi zajedno rješavali prije svega bilateralna pitanja, kako se ne bi moralo ići u Abu Dhabi. Voditeljica dodaje da to vrijedi bez obzira na to tko kupuje karte.
sections.subtitle_en: Clash of External Tutors in the Balkans: New Actors Oust the Old Ones
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest lists external powers fighting for influence in the region
sections.content_en:
There are an incredibly large number of external tutors in the region, points out Jadranka Polović, and some of them are weakening. She enumerates them:

- The **USA** and the **European Union**, present for 30 years now,
- **Russia**, which is "shifting around something in the region," but less and less,
- **Turkey**, a very serious actor,
- **Israel**, a new player that strongly influences conditions,
- **Great Britain**, which is often forgotten because it is always quiet.

New actors, says the guest, are ousting the old ones. In the region, a **clash** is ongoing in which the USA, Great Britain, Turkey, and Israel, although not on good terms with each other, strive to suppress the influence of the European Union, primarily of **Germany**. France is holding on, and Polović cites as proof that **Macron** recently hosted **Vučić**.

It would be very good, the guest believes, if Croatia were to **push the entry of Montenegro and Serbia into the European Union**. The entire area would thereby be geopolitically rounded off and stabilized. She advocates for far more agreements and meetings of leaders from the region who would jointly resolve primarily bilateral issues, so that one would not have to go to Abu Dhabi. The host adds that this holds true regardless of who is buying the tickets.

sections.subtitle: „Neka jedu kolače“: velika kriza na pomolu i poruka europskim liderima
sections.screenshot_description: Jadranka Polović upozorava na tiskani novac bez pokrića i moguće velike nemire
sections.content:
Za kraj voditeljica pita bi li velika **ekonomska kriza**, o kojoj svi govore, i **pucanje financijskog balona** mogli izvesti ljude na ulice diljem Europe. Podsjeća na rečenicu pripisanu **Mariji Antoaneti**, **„Neka jedu kolače“**, i pita tko bi je danas mogao izgovoriti a da ne završi na giljotini.

Jadranka Polović odgovara da europski lideri zapravo upravo to i govore. Kada ih se sluša, situacija djeluje fantastično: rastu BDP, plaće i mirovine, gradi se na sve strane, a Europska unija sklapa sporazume u ime daljnjeg prosperiteta. Promjene se ipak moraju dogoditi. Gošća vjeruje da će se **Alternativa za Njemačku** kroz lokalne parlamentarne izbore ozbiljno pozicionirati, a spominje i **Marine Le Pen** te moguće strukture desnije od **Meloni**. Pred Francuskom, Španjolskom i Italijom su izbori.

Polović nije sigurna da će ni nove snage moći riješiti nagomilane probleme, jer se sudaraju s vrlo lošom objektivnom situacijom. U opticaju je mnogo **tiskanog novca bez ikakve podloge**. Suočavanje s tom realnošću bilo bi strašno i moglo bi izazvati **velike nemire**, što je razlog njezine zabrinutosti za budućnost.

Voditeljica primjećuje da ta zabrinutost nije bez razloga i da gošća u njoj nije usamljena. Dodaje da kraj podcasta nije depresivan, nego realan, s čime se Polović slaže. U završnoj poruci ponavlja da bi europski lideri, bile to nove snage ili postojeće, trebali biti svjesni da je potreban **radikalan zaokret ekonomskih politika i politike općenito**.

Voditeljica to naziva njezinim pozivom na revoluciju. Gošća odgovara da se nada kako do revolucije neće doći, „jer znate, ona uvijek pomete prvo nas“. Voditeljica zahvaljuje na iznimno zanimljivom razgovoru i odjavljuje emisiju: **Jadranka Polović** bila je gošća podcasta **Mrežnica**.
sections.subtitle_en: "Let Them Eat Cake": A Great Crisis Looms and a Message to European Leaders
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jadranka Polović warns about printed money without backing and possible major unrest
sections.content_en:
In conclusion, the host asks whether the great **economic crisis**, which everyone is talking about, and the **bursting of the financial bubble** could bring people out into the streets across Europe. She recalls the sentence attributed to **Marie Antoinette**, **"Let them eat cake"**, and asks who today could utter it without ending up on the guillotine.

Jadranka Polović replies that European leaders are actually saying precisely that. When one listens to them, the situation appears fantastic: GDP, wages, and pensions are rising, construction is underway on all sides, and the European Union is concluding agreements in the name of further prosperity. Changes must nevertheless happen. The guest believes that **Alternative for Germany** will seriously position itself through local parliamentary elections, and she also mentions **Marine Le Pen** as well as possible structures further to the right than **Meloni**. Elections lie ahead for France, Spain, and Italy.

Polović is not sure that even new forces will be able to resolve the accumulated problems, because they collide with a very poor objective situation. In circulation there is a lot of **printed money without any backing whatsoever**. Facing that reality would be terrible and could cause **major unrest**, which is the reason for her concern for the future.

The host observes that this concern is not without reason and that the guest is not alone in it. She adds that the end of the podcast is not depressing, but realistic, with which Polović agrees. In her concluding message, she repeats that European leaders, whether new forces or existing ones, should be aware that a **radical turnaround in economic policies and politics in general** is necessary.

The host calls this her call for a revolution. The guest replies that she hopes a revolution will not come to pass, "because you know, it always sweeps us away first." The host gives thanks for an exceptionally interesting conversation and signs off the show: **Jadranka Polović** was the guest of the podcast **Mrežnica**.
